We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today.






ROLE OVERVIEW

Benchling is building a world-class Professional Services team to drive implementations for our rapidly expanding customer base. Implementation Managers work with our customers, from small Biotech startups to the largest BioPharmas in the world to develop a deep understanding of their R&D Processes, and roll out solutions that transform how their research teams work together.


To be successful in this role, you will leverage your scientific background, project management skills, and product expertise to drive successful implementations of the Benchling platform. You will work hand in hand with the research scientists at our customers, and teams throughout Benchling to implement our solutions, and ensure our customers are successful. Implementation Managers lead all aspects of customer rollouts from requirements analysis and solution design, to configurations, testing, training, and onboarding users onto the system.



You are fluent or native proficiency in French and have experience working with French speaking customers.



RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Manage initial rollouts for new Benchling customers as well as expansion projects with new teams or for new processes at existing customers

 - Own implementation success from project kickoff to go-live, leveraging strong project management skills, scientific expertise, and deep product knowledge.

 - Build and execute detailed project plans, own project activities, work with other team members to execute on project deliverables to ensure on time, on budget, high quality deployments.

 - Understand customers' scientific workflows and determine how Benchling can best be leveraged to meet their key business needs.

 - Lead requirements and design workshops, perform data modeling & application configuration, develop test plans and guide UAT execution, train and onboard users.

 - Act as a trusted advisor for customers, guiding them through the implementation ensuring they leverage and apply Benchling Best Practices.

 - Understand and document customer pain points, advocate for them internally to influence product changes.

 - Identify and work with sales on opportunities for account expansion post go-live.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - MS or Ph.D. in Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Immunology, Bioinformatics, Biological Engineering or a related field.

 - At least 2 years of experience in a lab or R&D setting, ideally in antibody discovery or strain engineering or process development. You must be able to empathize with scientists and quickly understand complicated scientific concepts.

 - Software Implementation experience, preferably with a SaaS software company.

 - Strong communication skills. You must be able to quickly and effectively connect with a range of stakeholders, including scientists, IT project leads, and executives.

 - Self-starter with the ability to be successful in a startup environment.

 - Curious, creative, and tenacious. You should be excited to collaborate with customers and other Benchling teammates as a thought partner.

 - Ability to travel up to 25% based on customer and project needs.

 - Experience using Benchling, especially if you’ve been a Benchling administrator, is preferred but not required.

 - Fluent or native proficiency in French

Benchling welcomes everyone.

We believe diversity enriches our team so we hire people with a wide range of identities, backgrounds, and experiences.

We are an equal opportunity employer. That means we don’t discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We also consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law, including but not limited to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

/job/Basel/Scientist-Synthesis-Automatio.description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position
In Roche’s Pharmaceutical Research and Early Development organization (pRED), we make transformative medicines for patients in order to tackle some of the world’s toughest unmet healthcare needs. At pRED, we are united by our mission to transform science into medicines. Together, we create a culture defined by curiosity, responsibility, and humility, where our talented people are empowered and inspired to bring forward extraordinary life-changing innovation at speed.

Therapeutic Modality (TMo) organization, accountable for translating disease biology into high-quality drug candidates across small molecules, large molecules, oligonucleotides, and genomic medicines. By integrating deep modality expertise with cross-disciplinary collaboration, TMo drives innovation within and across platforms to enable differentiated, sustainable therapeutic impact.

The Medicinal Chemistry Team in Pharma Research and Early Development, located in Basel, is part of Small Molecule Research. We are a community of drug hunters with expertise in synthesis, design and purification, with a responsibility to convert hypotheses into innovative small molecules for treating diseases of high unmet medical need, closely collaborating with our broader therapeutic areas and functions. In your role, you will be working on accelerating compound synthesis through automation and digitalization as part of the Dolphin team. You will be focusing on expanding and executing synthetic technologies (e.g., parallel chemistry and  late-stage functionalization). 
  
The opportunity
In your role as a Scientist within Medicinal Chemistry, you will be working on accelerating compound synthesis through automation and digitalization as part of the Dolphin team. You will be focusing on expanding and executing synthetic technologies (e.g., parallel chemistry and late-stage functionalization). This requires the introduction of new synthetic methodologies and techniques, including reaction miniaturization, photochemical transformations, small-scale purification and analytical methodology development. Thereby you will also contribute to generating high-quality reaction datasets for machine learning applications.

You devise and implement state-of-the-art scientific research by conducting laboratory experiments. By designing, planning and executing multi-step organic synthesis and purification of high-quality target molecules for biological screening you maintain a high level of productivity in the laboratory setting.

You predominantly design and run high-throughput experiments on a miniaturized scale using automation equipment. Thereby you continuously implement new methodologies and innovative technologies to expand the current capabilities.

You propose and implement innovative and pragmatic solutions to synthetic and technical problems.

You closely collaborate with project teams to influence and guide the opportunities of late-stage functionalization, library synthesis, and other digital and/or automation applications.

You work on cutting-edge innovation at the crossroads of automation, digitalization, medicinal chemistry and compound synthesis.

You coordinate an internal team and manage CRO teams in Europe and China.

You serve as a contact point for parallel synthesis between sites in Basel, Shanghai and San Francisco. 

Who you are
You possess a very strong background in synthetic organic chemistry and laboratory digitalization to accelerate the synthesis of chemical matter for Medicinal Chemistry, ideally with a PhD in Synthetic Organic Chemistry with at least four years of industry experience. In particular:

You have expertise in automation technology, including solid dosing and liquid handling, integrated with analytical and purification methodologies.

You have a strong background in synthetic methodology development and hands-on laboratory experimentation in small molecule synthesis.

You have experience in assessing and implementing digitalization and automation solutions in chemical laboratories.

You understand machine learning concepts for reaction prediction and have experience in collecting reaction datasets.

You have experience in applying parallel medicinal chemistry approaches to solve medicinal chemistry problems. 

You have experience in cross-functional and international relationship building within a large discovery organization including stakeholder management and academic collaborations.

You have demonstrated agile distribution and prioritization of work packages between internal and CRO-based teams

You have excellent communication and presentation skills, along with strong interpersonal abilities with a track record of leading matrix teams without positional authority.

At Roche, we aim high to deliver life-changing healthcare solutions. If you’re ready to make a meaningful impact on patients and healthcare systems worldwide, this is the place for you.

 
 

Who we are
A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.

Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Typical cryogenic systems comprise compressors, heat exchangers, valves, instrumentation, vacuum pumps, controls and various test benches for cables, magnets and RF cavities. Process gas purity is essential.

Votre activité comprend l’optimisation préopératoire, la prise en charge médicale durant l’hospitalisation et le suivi postopératoire, ainsi que la prévention, l’identification et le traitement des complications péri-opératoires.

Vous développez votre raisonnement clinique en étant confronté ou confrontée à des situations péri-opératoires variées, parfois complexes, tout en bénéficiant d’une supervision de proximité. 
Au sein d’un environnement universitaire et pluridisciplinaire, vous participez également à l’encadrement des médecins stagiaires et avez accès aux formations théoriques et pratiques proposées par les services de médecine interne générale et d’orthopédie. 
À ce titre, vous poursuivez votre formation postgraduée conformément aux exigences FMH. L’année effectuée est reconnue comme une année de formation postgraduée en orthopédie et peut être prise en compte dans le cursus menant au titre de spécialiste FMH en médecine interne générale.

En tant que cheffe ou chef de clinique titulaire du titre de spécialiste en médecine interne générale, vous rejoignez l’équipe de médecine péri-opératoire du Service de chirurgie orthopédique et traumatologie de l’appareil moteur. Vous contribuez à la prise en charge médicale globale des patientes et patients hospitalisés dans les différentes unités du service. 
En collaboration étroite avec les équipes chirurgicales, anesthésiologiques, infirmières et les autres professionnels impliqués, vous assurez l’évaluation, l’optimisation et le suivi des patientes et patients présentant des comorbidités ou des problématiques médicales péri-opératoires. 
Votre activité clinique comprend notamment l’évaluation médicale préopératoire, l’optimisation des pathologies aiguës et chroniques susceptibles d’influencer le risque opératoire ou la récupération, ainsi que la prévention, l’identification et la prise en charge des complications postopératoires. Vous participez aux visites interdisciplinaires et coordonnez les stratégies diagnostiques et thérapeutiques en lien avec les médecins adjoints et médecins adjointes ainsi que les équipes concernées. 
Vous supervisez les médecins internes dans leur activité quotidienne, les accompagnez dans leur raisonnement clinique et contribuez activement à leur formation. Vous veillez à la qualité de la documentation médicale, à la continuité des prises en charge et à la coordination du parcours hospitalier des patientes et patients. 
Grâce à votre sens clinique, à votre capacité de priorisation et à votre autonomie, vous gérez des situations variées, parfois complexes, dans un environnement hospitalier exigeant et interdisciplinaire. Vous entretenez une communication claire et constructive avec les équipes médico-soignantes, les patientes et patients ainsi que leurs proches. 
Vous participez enfin au développement et à la structuration de l’activité de médecine péri-opératoire en orthopédie, ainsi qu’aux projets d’amélioration de la qualité, d’enseignement et, selon les opportunités, de recherche clinique. 
L’activité est organisée principalement du lundi au vendredi, selon les besoins et le fonctionnement du service.

En tant que cheffe ou chef de clinique titulaire du titre de spécialiste en chirurgie orthopédique, vous rejoignez l’unité de chirurgie de la main dans le cadre d’une spécialisation. L’unité assure les urgences 24h/24 de la main et du poignet pour tout le canton de Genève (traitement des plaies, fractures du poignet ou des doigts, etc.) ainsi que les consultations dédiées pour différentes pathologies telles que l’arthrose de la main, le syndrome du canal (ou tunnel) carpien, la tendinite, etc.
Dans cette fonction, vous assurez une activité clinique complète, incluant les interventions chirurgicales et la prise en charge des patientes et patients intrahospitalier. Vous contribuez également activement aux projets de l’unité.
Vous faites preuve de rigueur, de sens clinique et d’une grande capacité d’analyse dans la prise en charge de situations parfois complexes, y compris dans la gestion des complications à court terme. Grâce à votre sens de l’organisation et à votre capacité à prioriser, vous assurez efficacement vos activités cliniques tout en répondant aux sollicitations multiples (patients et patientes, téléphones, correspondances, réunions).
Vous évoluez dans un environnement exigeant, à l’interface des soins, de l’enseignement et de la recherche. À ce titre, vous collaborez étroitement avec l’ensemble de l’équipe médico-soignante et veillez à une communication claire, fluide et respectueuse, tant avec vos collègues qu’avec les patientes et patients, en adaptant votre discours à leur compréhension.
En vous appuyant sur votre esprit d’équipe, vous faites preuve de solidarité face aux imprévus et aux charges de travail élevées. En tant que cheffe ou chef de clinique, vous participez activement à la supervision et à la formation des médecins internes, en adoptant une posture de mentorat et en partageant votre expertise.
Vous prenez part aux gardes de l’unité de chirurgie de la main.
L’activité clinique s’inscrit dans un parcours de formation postgraduée structuré et exigeant, visant la spécialisation en chirurgie de la main. Cet environnement offre des opportunités de développement reconnues, incluant des formations pratiques et théoriques de haut niveau, notamment à travers des collaborations avec la SFITS (Swiss Foundation for Innovation and Training in Surgery).

/job/Basel/Cardio-Renal-Discovery-Area-L.description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position
In Roche’s Pharmaceutical Research and Early Development organization (pRED), we make transformative medicines for patients in order to tackle some of the world’s toughest unmet healthcare needs. At pRED, we are united by our mission to transform science into medicines. Together, we create a culture defined by curiosity, responsibility, and humility, where our talented people are empowered and inspired to bring forward extraordinary life-changing innovation at speed.

pRED Cardiovascular & Metabolism, Immunology (CMI), located in Basel, Switzerland, focuses on the discovery and early development of innovative treatments for specific diseases that affect the lives of millions. In the cardiovascular and metabolism area, we are developing cutting-edge therapies to treat metabolic diseases. 

The Position
The Cardio-Renal Discovery Area Leader is a newly created and premier scientific leadership role within the CVRM therapeutic area, acting as the principal architect of the early-stage pipeline in cardiovascular and renal diseases. The focus is on pioneering novel cardiovascular and renal discovery programs and advancing them from target assessment through preclinical candidate selection . This role emphasizes deep, mechanistic disease expertise, leading an elite team of translational scientists and discovery biologists to interrogate the complex, interconnected biology of the cardiorenal axis.  
This role reports directly to the Discovery Head of CVRM. Key interactions include presenting high-level portfolio strategies to the Leadership Team and governance boards, as well as maintaining deep collaborative relationships with world-renowned scientists and academic networks in cardiology and nephrology. 

As a leader in CMI, you act as a catalyst for innovation, championing an enterprise mindset that prioritizes long-term scientific impact. You cultivate an environment of high performance and psychological safety, empowering elite teams of translational scientists to interrogate complex cardiorenal biology. Your leadership is defined by an unwavering commitment to integrity, courage, and passion, driving the organization to deliver transformative breakthroughs for patients.
 
Your key responsibilities will include:  

Novel Target Identification: Drive scientific strategy to validate disease-modifying targets across CV and renal segments.

Mechanistic Subspecialties: Champion programs targeting advanced mechanisms like myocardial energetics and podocyte injury.

Modality-Agnostic Innovation: Lead teams across small molecules, RNA-based therapeutics, and advanced biologics.

Phenotypic & Human-Centric Screening: Oversee 3D cardiac organoids and kidney-on-a-chip models.

Preclinical-to-Clinical Translation: Accountability for scientific integrity of preclinical pharmacology and design architecture for transitioning leads into IND/CTA-enabling packages.

Scouting & Due Diligence: Serve as technical authority for evaluating external assets and biotech platforms.

Scientific Eminence: Cultivate collaborative relationships with academic research networks and consortia.

Who You Are
You will bring 10+ years of progressive biopharmaceutical industry or premier academic translation experience, with a documented history of driving CV/renal assets from early concept to successful IND/CTA filing and FIH readiness.

Qualifications & Experience:

Education Level: PhD, MD, or MD/PhD in Cardiovascular Physiology, Renal Physiology, Pharmacology, Molecular Biology, or a highly relevant life sciences discipline.

Specialist Knowledge: Advanced authority on the pathophysiology of cardiorenal networks, including CKD/Nephropathy, Myocardial Remodeling & Fibrosis, the Cardiorenal Axis, Genetic & Rare Diseases, and Atherosclerosis & Lipid Metabolism.

Fluency in English (written and spoken) is required.

Unwavering focus, collaborative teamwork and exceptional delivery are key behaviours that drive our mission of doing now what patients need next. Together, we can be transformative
 
 

Who we are
A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.

Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

/job/Basel/Senior-Director--Medical-Affa.description:
BeOne continues to grow at a rapid pace with challenging and exciting opportunities for experienced professionals. When considering candidates, we look for scientific and business professionals who are highly motivated, collaborative, and most importantly, share our passionate interest in fighting cancer.

The Senior Medical Director Hemato-Oncology, Medical Affairs, Europe is the internal key expert within the indication area(s), directly supporting the respective products through development, pre-marketing, launch, marketing support and lifecycle management. This includes all areas of medical affairs activities such as support of safe and appropriate product use, data-generation, data-dissemination and HCP interactions. Subject matter expertise is essential.

The role is part of a matrix organization, reporting to the Executive Director Medical Affairs Europe, but with collaboration with the European Medical Affairs group, other Regional/Country Medical Directors and regional medical
affairs functions as well as Global Medical Affairs and Global Clinical Development Functions. It requires close interaction with local (country) medical directors with respect to allocated disease area(s) (Hematological malignancies) to assure strategic dialogue considering local specifics and input as well as regional guidance.

The Medical Director Hematology has accountability for the regional input into the product and indication strategies and works closely with local country medical directors to assure alignment across global, regional and local strategies, messaging as well as tactical implementation.

Reports To: Executive Medical Director, Regional Medical Lead Hemato-Oncology, Medical Affairs, Europe

The role includes, but is not limited to:
• Matrix leadership in the disease area
• Proactive contribution to regional and global brand and disease area strategies

Including gap analyses

Identification of areas of interest with respect to ISR

Publication planning

Regional data-dissemination (e.g. company sponsored symposia, congress submissions, medical education activities)

Regional HCP interactions / outreach (e.g. investigator meetings, advisory boards)
• Close collaboration with regional commercial teams regarding pre-launch, launch and commercialization support, assuring timely medical input and accuracy of medical / scientific content

As a subject matter expert for the assigned disease area, the incumbent will be accountable to develop regional strategies to support enduring and compliant relationships with Opinion Leaders, Research Collaborators, and Key
Organizations in support of BeOne’s pipeline development across the allocated disease area.
The incumbent will play a key role in the establishment of BeOne as a valued collaborator and best-in-class biopharmaceutical company.

Essential Functions of the job:
• Establish and maintain scientifically credible peer-to-peer scientific relationships with key national & regional
opinion leaders in addition to other healthcare providers
• Viewed as a Scientific Partner by KOLs
• Facilitate & monitor strategic partnerships with scientific/clinical experts and serve as a regional-level point of contact with organizations including but not limited to -

Guideline development

Cooperative groups

Other (Regional / National Cancer institutions)
• Facilitate & monitor strategic partnerships with other functional areas within BeOne
• Leadership in the development and execution of clinically relevant regional medical meetings (e.g., advisory boards, consultant, and investigator meetings), as requested
• Develop, track, execute and report on goals and objectives.
• Support disease area Medical Affairs budget planning and management.
• Be accountable for compliant business practices.

Experience:
• MD, with relevant clinical / scientific experience in the indication field
• Minimum 10 years of experience and success within other biotech/pharmaceutical companies.
• Track record of experience (clinical and industry) in the field of Hemato-Oncology
• High level of communication (written and verbal), interpersonal, organizational, and cross functional collaboration skills.
• Flexibility to work with colleagues in a global setting.
• Able to engage in work-related travel approximately 50%.

Capabilities and Competencies:
• Impactful verbal and written communication skills.
• Ability to effectively collaborate in a dynamic environment.
• Strong comprehension of disease states, and knowledge of differential algorithms for treatment decisions and experience in disease states of interest to BeOne.
• An expert understanding of the health care delivery system, including the managed care arena and its impact on patient care, regional medical care and the pharmaceutical industry. Ability to identify the unmet medical, educational, and research needs at a local & regional level in the medical community.
• Ability to interpret key scientific data and translate the findings to meet educational and research needs to affect corporate research strategic activities/decisions.
• Understanding of the design and execution of research studies and strategic implications.
• Exhibits high degree of emotional intelligence and appreciation of diversity and multiculturalism.
• Designs and/or leads training initiatives and best practices.
• Proven ability to drive results at a high level of quality as a strategic and creative thinker.
• Demonstrates ability to deal with ambiguity and thrive in an ever-changing environment.
• Strong project management skills with demonstrated ability to manage projects and/or colleagues in successful implementation of business-critical projects.
• Strong time management & organizational skills

Education Required:
Medical Doctor (MD) degree or PHD or equivalent medical qualification required with relevant clinical / scientific experience in the indication field as well as industry experience and managerial track record required.

Supervisory Responsibilities:
• Initially, there will be no direct reports
• As the portfolio in the disease area expands regional medical resources will need to increase leading to supervisory responsibilities within the disease area

Computer Skills:
• Proficient in Microsoft Office
• Experienced with electronic CRM systems

Other Qualifications:
• Fluent in English (written and spoken)
• Other European languages are an advantage

Travel:
• A significant amount of travel is expected
• Participation at major congresses

Self-Awareness
Acts Inclusively
Demonstrates Initiative
Entrepreneurial Mindset
Continuous Learning
Embraces Change
Results-Oriented
Analytical Thinking/Data Analysis
Financial Excellence

/job/Basel/Portfolio-Strategy---Delivery.description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position
 
In Roche’s Pharmaceutical Research and Early Development organisation (pRED), we make transformative medicines for patients to tackle some of the world’s toughest unmet healthcare needs. At pRED, we are united by our mission to transform science into medicines. Together, we create a culture defined by curiosity, responsibility, and humility, where our talented people are empowered and inspired to bring forward extraordinary, life-changing innovation at speed.

Strategy, Portfolio & Operations (SPO) is a unified function that serves as the strategic and operational backbone enabling pRED's strategy from lab to clinic. Operating under a dynamic Chapter Model, SPO centralises specialised skills across critical areas, including Sites & Lab Services, Program & Project Management, Strategy, Clinical Operations, External Operations, Capability Development, Core Lab Technology Platforms (360Labs) and Asset Team Leadership. SPO’s mission is to drive enterprise value creation by delivering operational excellence and accelerating portfolio productivity. As a trusted partner, SPO fosters a culture of collaboration and accountability to ensure pRED transitions assets smoothly from early research to late-stage development. 

At Roche/Genentech Pharma Research and Early Development Clinical Operations (pRED CO), we are determined to transform early drug development and realise our Pharma Ambition to deliver 20 transformative medicines addressing diseases with the highest societal burden by 2029. The pRED Portfolio Strategy & Delivery Lead leads the delivery of one or more of our Discovery & Delivery Areas (DTAs), driving productivity, efficiency and innovation. This senior people leadership position holds significant accountability for the pRED Clinical Operations strategy and execution, as well as enterprise collaboration.

The Opportunity

The pRED Portfolio Strategy & Delivery Lead is a senior strategic leader and decision-maker within Roche pRED Clinical Operations and is responsible and accountable for shaping an industry-leading CO DTA strategy that successfully delivers the pRED portfolio of programs and studies in the assigned DTA(s).  Leads the functional area of responsibility (Asset, Study Management, Data & Technology or People), driving the identification and development of new ways of working to push the boundaries of excellence in delivery and engagement continually.  As the DTA Portfolio Strategy & Delivery Lead, you will:

Build, drive, and enhance cross-functional enterprise collaborations and influence decision-making across early- and late-stage development, while providing a strong strategic operational voice to remove barriers and align on priorities.

pRED: Partner with Early Development Heads and Project Team Leaders to translate eSPC and DTA strategies into a coherent pRED CO delivery portfolio strategy that balances business needs with budgets and resources. Serve as the primary decision-maker for prioritising strategic operational DTA decisions, collaborating across early and late-stage teams to optimise day-to-day execution. Additionally, leverage data analytics, informatics, and AI to drive data-driven decision-making, while working cross-functionally with CO leadership to refine delivery strategies, overcome performance challenges, and enhance both operational efficiency and employee engagement. 
PD, gRED and Roche Enterprise: As the voice for pRED in your therapeutic area(s) you must proactively identify, develop, and maintain collaborative relationships with senior leaders across the Roche Enterprise to ensure early development representation and influence for the end-to-end delivery of the portfolio, including late-stage Development and Roche Diagnostics. ,
External Stakeholders:  Proactively identify, develop, and maintain collaborative relationships with key external partners including patient advocacy organisations, Therapeutic Area Experts (TAE), Health Authorities, vendors in accordance with our sourcing strategy, and key development partners. 

By exemplifying our Roche values and Leadership commitments and modelling our Roche Operating principles, you will ensure we achieve our ambitions for our people and patients. As an experienced People Leader, your accountabilities include:

Functional Responsibility: Lead one of the functional areas of responsibility (Asset, Study Management, Data & Technology or People*) to foster a culture and mindset of performance delivery, ownership and innovation. Inspire the identification and development of new ways of working to push the boundaries of excellence in delivery and engagement continually.
Capability Building: Articulate the strategic direction for your functional area of responsibility with a strong focus on talent development, effective resource deployment, and future capability development to meet the future needs of a dynamic portfolio.
Transformation: Lead change management to embed new operating models that increase productivity, speed and quality for pRED CO and across the CO Enterprise that realise our ambition of an industry-leading organisation.
Engagement & Collaboration: Drive CO-wide engagement by fostering a culture of collaboration, inclusivity, and high performance. Inspire, motivate, and develop talent within the team, ensuring a focus on individual growth and leadership development to build a strong, elevated talent pipeline aligned with organisational objectives.
Performance Management: Regular year-round assessment of performance, contributions, and impact and providing feedback, coaching and performance management.
People Leadership: Lead and develop a matrixed organisation of employees, including direct reports who may be people leaders themselves. Support all perspectives and seek out input from underrepresented voices. Provide opportunities for growth and development for all team members and address any barriers that may exist.  People management-related administration (e.g. Workday People & Culture Management system tasks) and contact for employment-related matters.
Operational & Strategic Leadership: Lead the functional area of responsibility to understand current performance, challenges and opportunities associated with Clinical Program/Study delivery and organisational model and formulate actionable solutions, in collaboration across functional areas and beyond to enhance delivery and engagement.
​Knowledge Management & Network Building: Knowledge management: develop a strong network of expertise from across the enterprise that can be leveraged to benefit the area of responsibility and across CO. This will also require the postholder to have a highly robust knowledge of the changing internal/external pressures and potential external partners to leverage.

Who You Are

You hold a university degree or equivalent years of experience (preferred focus in life sciences) with 15+ years of pharmaceutical clinical Operations experience, including at least 10 years in global clinical operations Strategy Leadership.
You are talented, passionate, an excellent communicator, and inspired by our mission. You will fit in well with our collaborative, patient-centric, and entrepreneurial spirit, possessing a growth mindset and an excitement for learning through experience.
You bring a comprehensive understanding of global Pharma early Clinical development in international settings, alongside strong knowledge in the area of CO, including external trends and issues in the global industry and competitive

/job/Basel/RiSM-Internship-for-students-.description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position
Pharmaceutical & Solid State Development is part of Pharma Technical Development and is situated in Basel, Switzerland. 
Our key expertise is the development of robust and economic processes for drug substances with tailor-made solid-state properties and patient-centric formulations for the synthetic molecule portfolio of projects from early clinical studies to commercialization. We advance the design and delivery of transformative medicines by combining particle engineering, characterization, and formulation development - ensuring optimal drug performance, manufacturability, and patient-centric solutions from molecule to medicine. 
As an intern, you will support the Pharmaceutical & Solid State Development department by driving our digital transformation, shifting the focus from building isolated, ad hoc tools to integrating, expanding, and supporting a single centralized digital interface. You will play a key role in consolidating existing applications and data products into a cohesive ecosystem aligned with our core scientific and business workflows, providing our science teams with a streamlined, digital-first operational environment.

The Opportunity

Interface Unification: Consolidate existing standalone digital applications into a single, cohesive user interface structured around specific pharmaceutical development business logic.

Feature Support & Optimization: Maintain the unified platform, implement critical upgrades, and develop newly requested features within the existing ecosystem rather than creating disconnected tools.

Advanced Data Engineering: Design and build reliable data pipelines, robust data products, and secure backend integrations to ensure seamless, high-performance data flow across the central platform.

Sustainability & Code Auditing: Audit, refactor, and restructure legacy codebase to meet enterprise-level standards for scalability, documentation, and reliable operational handovers.

AI-Ready Architecture: Set up an AI-ready unified application and data architecture designed for seamless future integration with Roche internal agentic AI tools.

Collaboration & Workflow Mapping: Translate complex scientific workflows and processes into structured, digitalrequirements by collaborating closely with scientists and project owners.

Who you are

You are a University student (or you graduated within 12 months before the start date)  in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, Bioinformatics, or a related technical discipline, with a strong interest in applying software engineering and data pipelines to scientific and pharmaceutical development challenges.
Furthermore, you are interested in using and sharing your knowledge as part of your Internship in a modern working environment. Your further profile for this position:

Advanced Programming & Full-Stack Development: Strong proficiency in full-stack web development, framework expertise (e.g., modern frontend/backend frameworks), API design, and clean software architecture.

Data Science & Engineering: Experience in core data engineering, automating robust data pipelines, and embedding analytical models directly into frontend systems.

Systems Thinking: Proven ability to translate complex scientific workflows and business logic into structured, user-friendly digital solutions.

Software Sustainability: Familiarity with version control (Git), code auditing, and writing clean, scalable, and fully documented code.

Self-sufficient & Collaborative: A team-oriented, problem-solving personality with self-sufficient work habits and a passion for working in a multidisciplinary environment.

Communication: Excellent proficiency in English; ability to communicate complex technical concepts to non-technical scientific stakeholders.

This internship opportunity is one of a number of positions we offer in the department per semester and is not suitable for writing a Bachelor/Master/Diploma thesis. 
The interviews will take place on an interview day with all considered candidates and representatives of the department.
Your complete application includes the following documents:

A Current CV and a Motivation Letter

For Non-EU/EFTA citizens: Due to regulations, you must provide a certificate issued by your university stating that an Internship is mandatory for your studies and you must be enrolled during the entire duration of the internship

The RiSM task (see below)

A certificate of enrollment (if you are currently studying)

Application process

The application deadline is 23.08.2026. All successful final candidates will be invited to a virtual interview day which will take place on 14.10.2026.
The Internship will start in May to July 2027 and has a duration of 9 to 12 months (alignedwith the project duration, please indicate your preferred start date and availability in yourapplication)
More information about the Roche Internship program in Synthetic Molecules (RiSM) and other opportunities within this program you can find here.

Are you ready to apply? We are looking for someone who thinks beyond the job offered - someone who knows that this position can be a rare springboard to many other opportunities

Additional information  (RISM Task)

Assume you are a software and data engineer tasked with unifying multiple fragmented, legacy tools into a central platform.
Please outline a technical proposal (maximum of 3 slides or 2 pages in PDF format) detailing your architectural strategy for:
1. How would you structure the unified frontend interface to accommodate diverse workflows
without creating visual clutter.
2. Your approach to building automated, robust, and scalable data pipelines that bring legacy data into the central system.
3. How would you structure the backend and data layers to ensure they are "AI-ready" for integration with internal agentic AI tools.
We anticipate receiving your technical strategy alongside your application.
 
 

Who we are
A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.

Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
/job/Basel/RiSM-Internship-for-students-.title: RiSM Internship for students in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science or Bioinformatics (Basel, 9-12 months)

Introduction
Within the CERN Engineering department (EN), the Electrical Engineering (EL) group is responsible for managing CERN’s electrical distribution network, ranging from 400 kV to 400/230 V, which includes its operation, maintenance, renovation, control as well as forecasting energy consumption and handling relations with suppliers. Additionally, the group oversees the cabling infrastructure, managing everything from the installation and removal of control, water-cooled, and fiber optic cables to the maintenance of their supporting structures.

You will join the Maintenance and Operation (EN-EL-MO) section, responsible for the operation and maintenance of CERN’s electrical network, the commissioning of new installations, and the execution of small-scale electrical works.
As an experienced industrial electrical technician in the EN-EL-MO section, you will be responsible for operating and maintaining part of CERN's high- and low-voltage electrical network. 
Apply your expertise to support the operation, maintenance, consolidation and development of CERN’s electrical transmission and distribution systems, the backbone of one of the world’s largest and most powerful particle colliders. Join the CERN electrical engineering team. Take part!
Functions
As responsible for maintaining and operating a portion of CERN's electrical network, you will:
Operate the high- and low-voltage network (lockouts, switching electrical equipment on and off, network reconfiguration).
Perform troubleshooting and repairs, document interventions, and lead or contribute to the preparation of technical reports.
Carry out regular inspections to ensure the reliability and safety of the electrical network.
Act as the contact person for users connected to the electrical network within the assigned area.
Supervise preventive and corrective maintenance activities, as well as electrical works.
Contribute to electrical projects executed by the Group: participate in project meetings, assist in the definition of technical solutions, prepare and execute tests and commissioning activities, and perform acceptance tests on high- and low-voltage installations.
Maintain accurate records of maintenance and operational activities, including work performed, issues encountered, and corrective actions taken.

Vous participez, avec les préparatrices et préparateurs en pharmacie, les logisticiens et logisticiennes et les assistantes et assistants en pharmacie, à l’activité de pharmacien ou pharmacienne de routine de l’Unité de logistique pharmaceutique de la pharmacie des HUG. Vous assurez, sous la supervision des pharmaciennes et pharmaciens chefs de projets et adjoints ou adjointes, au bon fonctionnement de l’approvisionnement en médicaments et leur mise à disposition auprès des patients.
En collaboration avec deux autres pharmaciens et pharmaciennes, vous êtes le ou la référente pour les demandes diverses des médecins et unités de soins en lien avec l’obtention des médicaments, vous supervisez la gestion des ruptures, vous gérez les stocks de stupéfiants illicites. Vous assurez le suivi des prescriptions des médicaments critiques. Vous pilotez le processus de contrôle et retrait de lots avec le responsable assurance qualité.
Vous garantissez la mise en application de la politique du médicament et des procédures de qualité et de sécurité. Vous contribuez à l’amélioration continue de l’organisation, en collaboration étroite avec les autres pharmaciens et pharmaciennes de l’unité, y compris en participant aux séances transversales avec d’autres unités ou services (pharmacie clinique, production).
Vous participez à la formation et l’encadrement de collaboratrices et collaborateurs de la Pharmacie y compris apprenants et apprenantes (MAS, stagiaires).

What you'll do
You will join one of CERN’s experimental physics groups, if selected for this Research Fellowship, to develop and lead your own research programme at the frontier of particle physics. You will work in a highly collaborative and international environment, analysing data, contributing to detector design, construction and/or operations, and engaging in the design, execution and interpretation of physics data analyses. You will also be part of CERN’s vibrant scientific community through seminars, workshops, training activities and collaborative projects.
Your key tasks
You conduct research in experimental physics within a CERN research group of your choice.
You contribute to CERN’s experimental physics programme using its large-scale scientific instruments.
You collaborate with physicists and engineers on studies of particle interactions and related research activities.
You develop and pursue your research interests within the framework of the Fellowship.
Your profile
You hold a strong background in experimental particle physics or a closely related field.
You have research experience aligned with the scientific activities carried out at CERN’s experimental facilities.
You are motivated to join a research group and contribute to high-impact scientific work.
You are eager to develop and pursue your own research interests within the Fellowship framework.
Your skills
You have solid analytical and problem-solving skills in the context of experimental physics.
You are able to work collaboratively within large, international scientific teams.
You communicate effectively in a scientific environment, including presenting and discussing research results.
You can work independently while contributing to shared research objectives and collaborative projects.

You will be joining the COE section (Communication, Outreach and Education), part of the Department Infrastructure group (IT-DI). IT-DI provides services to the department ranging from the architecture and the deployment of the CERN computing facilities to the laboratory computing security and the relations with the CERN user communities and general public.
The COE section needs your help to bring the world's largest physics laboratory closer to the scientific community, to students and trainees and to the general public.

Be part of the activities of the IT-DI-COE section in the areas of Education, Communication and Outreach.
Take an active part in restructuring the CERN IT website: support the completion of its WordPress migration and design a new information architecture to improve searchability and usability for diverse audiences, including CERN staff, researchers, and key global initiatives like the Worldwide LHC Computing Grid.
Support IT-DI-COE in event organisation, notably being part of the back office for the events like Conferences, Project events, CERN OpenDays (CERN IT part). This task includes the streamlining and the improvement of existing processes.

Au sein de la Maison OBB et dans le cadre d’une prise en charge pluridisciplinaire et pluri-hebdomadaire, vous assurez de manière autonome la prise en soins psychomotrice (bilan, séances individuelles et/ou groupale à médiation corporelle) d’enfants de 0 à 2 ans et leurs parents.
Vous accompagnez et soutenez la parentalité, le développement psychomoteur de l’enfant et la relation parent-enfant. 
Vous participez aux réunions de synthèse, à l’élaboration de projets thérapeutiques et d’orientation.
Au sein de la Maison OBB, une structure rattachée à l’Office de l’enfance et de la jeunesse, s’adressant prioritairement à des familles particulièrement vulnérables, vous avez la possibilité d'offrir un accompagnement dans le développement des liens parent-enfant auprès des familles à haut risque psychosocial.
Vous effectuez des évaluations psychomotrices puis un accompagnement parent-bébé dans une collaboration étroite avec l’équipe de la Maison OBB (équipe éducative de la FOJ) et celle du SPEA/HUG (pédopsychologue, pédopsychiatre de l’unité Guidance petite enfance, pédiatre, psychiatre adulte et assistante sociale).
En outre, vous soutenez et évaluez l’établissement des liens parent-bébé/enfant au cours des soins quotidiens (bain, change, repas, sommeil, interactions/jeux…) et les compétences du bébé/enfant ainsi que son développement psychomoteur en accompagnant ses parents dans la lecture, le décodage et les réponses à ses signaux.
Vous soutenez et accompagnez le parent selon son état psychique (dépression post-partum, trouble de la personnalité, trouble psychiatrique non-décompensé…).
De plus, vous soutenez et évaluez les compétences parentales.
Vous pouvez participer à des entretiens conjoint avec la ou le médecin pédopsychiatre ou psychologue.
Une participation est également demandée aux colloques d’équipe, aux supervisions, aux réseaux psycho-sociaux autour de la famille
Enfin, sur le plan administratif, vous vous chargez des notes de suite des observations quotidiennes de l’enfant et de la relation parent-bébé pour chaque famille. Vous participez à l’élaboration et la rédaction de rapports ainsi qu'à la facturation.

Vous rejoignez l’équipe de Malatavie-Unité de crise, qui propose un suivi de crise pour les 13-18 ans présentant un risque suicidaire et pouvant s'engager dans une prise en charge spécifique.
Vous contribuez au travail d’accueil et d’orientation des adolescents et adolescentes, ainsi que des jeunes adultes qui ont des pensées suicidaires et un mal-être important (entretiens d’accueil et d’orientation, évaluation du risque suicidaires, répondre à la Ligne Ados, répondre aux demandes reçues par mail et répondre aux questions posées par les jeunes sur la thématique du suicide via les plateformes Ciao.ch et on tecoute.ch).
En tant que psychologue de l’équipe Prévention, vous participez aux supervisions, aux différents temps de réunions et présentez les situations cliniques auprès de vos collègues.
Vous travaillez également en lien étroit avec le réseau genevois.
Vous pouvez donner des enseignements ainsi que des formations sur la question de la Prévention du risque suicidaire.

We are looking for a passionate DevOps Engineer to join the CERN IT Storage and Data Management group (IT-SD).
Our group operates the core services used by LHC and non-LHC experiments to store and manage their data, to enable data archival, reconstruction and analysis and to distribute them to archiving and computing facilities around the world (Worldwide LHC Computing Grid). The group also contributes to data management services operated in the LHC experiments.
If you are excited about distributed systems, exabyte-scale data, and the future of distributed computing, this is the place for you.
You will be working on scientific data management technologies (Rucio, FTS, ...). Rucio is the facto data management platform in HEP and other sciences, managing over one exabyte of data across hundreds of data centers worldwide.
Computing power needs are evolving, especially for the HL-LHC, and researchers are increasingly relying on massive supercomputers and their capacity to run computations and AI workflows.
To support this, Rucio is expected to act as a bridge between our distributed data systems and these remote supercomputers, ensuring datasets are moved seamlessly to where the heavy processing happens, and results flow back to the scientific community.
Your responsibilities:
You will work on a project that federates massive compute and storage resources across Europe, enabling seamless cross-border scientific collaboration.
Your key responsibilities will include:
Connecting data to AI factories: Build integrations that allow large datasets to be easily accessed and utilised by next-generation European AI Factories and supercomputers.
Building a storage federation: Design and validate systems that allow different data management platforms to communicate among themselves, ensuring transparent data access and policy-driven replication.
Contributing to open source: Design robust new functionality and commit your code, features, and fixes directly back to the upstream Rucio project.
Supporting the community: Actively participate in our Operations team to maintain infrastructure for EU projects and activities surrounding the Rucio service, including troubleshooting incidents and supporting our users.
Your profile:
Demonstrated experience in:
Software development and integration (Python, scripting).
Linux system administration, configuration and automation, both in baremetal and container environments (Kubernetes).
Development tools (Git) and modern devops practices.
Working in teams.
Skills:
We are looking for someone who enjoys problem-solving at scale and loves working in a collaborative, open-source environment.
Strong Python programming and API design.
Linux system administration and Kubernetes clusters.
Solid understanding of large-scale data management, storage systems, or cloud environments.
Familiarity with authentication mechanisms and secure data transfers is a big plus.
A user-focused mindset and a willingness to jump into daily operations and user support.
Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the basics of the other language.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Computing Engineer (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is either a Bachelor's or Master's degree.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.
Applicants without University degree are not eligible.
Applicants with a PhD are not eligible.

We are looking for a passionate Computing Engineer to join CERN's IT Storage and Data Management group (IT-SD). Our group enables large-scale data access for the laboratory, the Large Hadron Collider and CERN's broader experimental programme, managing more than one exabyte of storage in the CERN Data Centre.
You will join the CERNBox team, which provides cloud storage to the CERN community and is making CERNBox interoperable and deployable across European research infrastructures and the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) Federation. You will package, test and validate the stack using Kubernetes and Helm for deployment across on-premises and public clouds, and contribute to Reva, its Go-based backend, by implementing the Open Cloud Mesh (OCM) protocol, an emerging IETF standard for interoperable cloud storage and data sharing across institutions.
If you are excited about cloud-native systems, open standards and building software adopted by research institutions worldwide, this is the place for you!
Your responsibilities
Develop and integrate backend software components.
Package and deploy interoperable services in distributed environments.
Support CERN community: you will join our operations team, troubleshooting incidents and supporting users.
Contribute your code, features and fixes back to the CERNBox open-source projects, working alongside a broader open-source community.
Work with partner institutions and research infrastructures across Europe to test, validate and refine these tools together.
Support users and partner teams as they adopt these tools, helping with troubleshooting and guidance.
Your profile
Experience, or a strong interest, in backend development and cloud-native deployment.
Enjoys troubleshooting, hands-on problem-solving, user support and service management.
Comfortable collaborating with external partners and international teams.
Curiosity about system integration and interoperability challenges.
Skills
Kubernetes and Helm chart development.
Backend software development, in particular Go.
Linux tech stack, administration and automation.
Nice to have: frontend development.
Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the basics of the other language.

You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Computer Engineering (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is either a Bachelor's or Master's degree.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.
Applicants without University degree are not eligible.
Applicants with a PhD are not eligible.

Are you passionate about digital design, digital signal processing, and experimental accelerator physics? Do you want to contribute to the modernisation of CERN's advanced linear accelerators? If so, this is an exceptional opportunity to bridge laboratory innovations with hands-on commissioning at a world-class facility.
In this role, you will join the Accelerator Systems Department (SY) and work within the Radio Frequency (RF) Group. The group is responsible for the design, operation, and maintenance of the RF acceleration and deflecting systems across the entire CERN accelerator complex. As part of an ongoing consolidation and performance upgrade Low-Level Radio Frequency (LLRF) systems are being modernised. You will contribute directly to the design, prototyping, and implementation of a next-generation digital LLRF cavity controller.
Your responsibilities:
Develop FPGA firmware implementing precise real-time phase, amplitude, and resonance tuning algorithms.
Design and integrate firmware components and fast diagnostic sub-systems.
Develop Python-based tools and frameworks for automated hardware testing, parameter characterisation, and laboratory data analysis.
Support the integration, laboratory validation, and commissioning of the new low-level cavity controllers directly.
More information here.
Your profile:
Required experience:
Experience in FPGA design and firmware development, preferably using VHDL.
Familiarity with FPGA development environments and verification/debugging tools.
Programming experience in Python or a similar language for test automation and data analysis.
Desired experience:
Experience modeling or simulating digital signal processing (DSP) algorithms or control loops.
Exposure to Radio Frequency (RF) concepts, basic control theory (like PID loops), or electronics hardware debugging.
Familiarity with hardware testing and developing automated test benches for hardware validation.
Skills:
Required Skills:
Proficiency in digital design and FPGA development, ideally utilising VHDL or Verilog.
Solid programming skills in Python.
Ability to troubleshoot and validate mixed-signal hardware systems.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Desired Skills:
Knowledge of digital signal processing techniques, such as digital filtering, mixing, or I/Q modulation/demodulation.
Understanding of basic feedback control systems and control theory.
Familiarity with version control workflows using Git and continuous integration (CI).
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
You have a professional background in Electronics Engineering (or a related field) and have either:
a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;
or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

Introduction:
You will play a key role in building meaningful relationships with CERN’s current and prospective donors throughout the entire donor cycle, while managing formal obligations such as proposal preparation and reporting. In doing so, you will help generate financial and strategic support for CERN by identifying funding opportunities, securing donations and grants, and building partnerships with corporations and foundations.
Functions:
Development and implementation of fundraising strategies for CERN fundraising projects.
Identification, qualification, cultivation, and stewardship of donors, including planning and conducting of donor meetings, events, and experiences.
Research and pursue of funding opportunities with foundations, including writing proposals and reports.
Track, analyse, and report on fundraising performance and partnership impact.
Collaborate with internal teams to align fundraising with project goals, prepare donor agreements and reports.
Conceptualise and produce communications materials for fundraising purposes.
Support Due Diligence process.

As a Construction Project Engineer within the Site and Civil Engineering Department (Project Portfolio Management Group), you will contribute to the delivery of complex construction projects at CERN. Reporting to a CERN Project Manager, you will coordinate site activities, manage interfaces with internal and external stakeholders, and ensure smooth execution while meeting technical, scheduling, budgetary, and safety objectives
Your responsibilities
Supervise the execution of construction works and ensure, in liaison with the relevant external consultants (architects, structural and MEP engineers), that all works comply with contractual drawings and specifications.
Ensure that all safety measures are properly implemented and adhered to on the worksites, while identifying potential issues, preventing their occurrence and managing the remediation of defects.

Job Description

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

This position is part of the Microbiological Quality Control (MBQC) team from Thermo Fisher Scientific in Lengnau (CH), supporting GMP-regulated manufacturing operations. At least 5 years experience in microbiological laboratories including experience in a regulated GMP environment.

Extensive knowledge of microbiological testing techniques (bioburden, endotoxin, qPCR) and laboratory best practices

Lead global translational teams across Phase I–IIa (“Discovery” through TDP), driving implementation of high‑quality development strategies in single or multiple neurodegeneration indications.
Represent TM on global program teams (GPT) and decision boards, ensuring that neurodegeneration programs meet quality, regulatory, and differentiation objectives.

Contribute to opportunity assessments and due diligence for neurodegeneration and adjacent therapeutic areas.

Governance, Compliance & Documentation

MD and PhD required with clinical subspecialty training in neurological diseases with deep expertise in neurodegeneration disorders

As a Therapeutic Area Biomarker Lead (TABL) in the Biomarker Development (BMD) group, you are accountable for defining and delivering biomarker strategies for the Immunology portfolio across multiple drug development programs in early and late clinical stages. You are accountable to translate the preclinical mechanistic understanding into an indication-relevant biomarker strategy, a clinical fit-for-purpose biomarker plan, oversee the integration into the clinical protocol, and lead the scientific and strategic discussions in project teams and governance meetings. As such you are a key member of global project teams, lead the Biomarker and Diagnostic teams, engage in Translational Data Science teams, and provide scientific, strategic, and tactical input aligned to the portfolio.

In the late phase particularly, you will be expected to assume the overall accountability for the biomarker strategy for at least one of our portfolio assets.

Furthermore, you will be leading overarching asset-related biomarker strategies enabling the delivery of late phase assets and respective launches.

Accountable for the biomarker strategy at a project, indication and study level in coordination with the respective clinical study lead and biomarker study expert.
Lead a dedicated matrixed group of biomarker subject matter experts and project team representatives to align key stakeholders on the biomarker strategy and biomarker plan at the project and study level and across the portfolio.
Accountable for the concept, endorsement, implementation, delivery and contextualization of the biomarker strategy.

Co-leads strategic translational data science working groups focused on integrating large-scale molecular and clinical patient data sets to identify novel indications, patient subgroups, and endpoints to enable decision-making.
Providing thought leadership with other BMD TABLs to identify synergies and drive innovation across our large and diverse clinical portfolio in immunology and general medicine.
Representing BMD on early and late Disease Area Initiatives or Consortia to identify, develop, and drive disease and compound mechanistic biology, clinical decision-making exploratory biomarkers and precision medicine hypotheses for the portfolio.

Job Description SummaryThe Senior Data Scientist & Scientific Software Engineer will join the Modeling & Simulation Data Science team within the Translational Medicine Unit to help advance data-driven drug discovery. The role is focused on transforming large-scale ADME, PK, and related experimental datasets into actionable insights through advanced analytics, machine learning, and robust software engineering. Partnering closely with pharmacokinetic sciences (PKS) scientists, Data & Digital teams, and cross-functional stakeholders, this position will drive the development of scalable analytical applications, reusable computational workflows, and decision-enabling in silico solutions that accelerate lead optimization and strengthen scientific decision making.

 
Job Description
200+ experimental datasets are generated every day in the Pharmacokinetic Sciences (PKS) department at Novartis Biomedical Research. This role sits at the center of efforts to unlock the value of these data for decision making and to shape the future of medicine through advanced data science.
As Associate Director Data Scientist & Scientific Software Engineer, you will join the Modeling & Simulation Data Science team in the Translational Medicine Unit and work at the intersection of data science, software engineering, and drug discovery. You will apply machine learning, statistics, and modern software development practices to harness ADME and PK data, uncover structure–property relationships, and translate scientific and business needs into scalable, strategically aligned solutions.
You will collaborate closely with Data & Digital and PKS wet- (ADME and bioanalytical) and dry-lab (modeling) teams to identify opportunities where data, applications, and in silico methods can meaningfully improve decision quality, efficiency, and scientific impact. In addition to hands-on technical delivery, you will help shape and champion fit-for-purpose solutions that are robust, reusable, and maintainable in a production setting.
This role is ideal for a scientifically grounded data leader who combines strong analytical depth with practical software engineering expertise, and who is motivated by delivering measurable impact in drug discovery through high-quality data products, machine learning, and computational innovation.

Key Responsibilities

Act as a key Modeling & Simulation Data Science representative on discovery and lead optimization programs, contributing scientific and strategic input to project discussions and decisions.

Partner with Data & Digital and PKS wet- and dry-lab teams to identify priority gaps, clarify business needs, and translate them into high-impact analytical and computational solutions.

Design, build, and maintain scalable applications, workflows, and data pipelines that support scientific analysis and decision making across projects and modalities.

Develop, evaluate, and deploy machine learning and statistical models to uncover relationships between chemical structure and molecular or pharmacokinetic properties.

Apply data mining, visualization, and exploratory analysis to derive insight from complex experimental datasets and communicate findings clearly to diverse stakeholders.

Create and implement project- or modality-specific in silico models and data strategies that accelerate and streamline compound progression decisions.

Write production-quality code following strong software engineering practices, including version control, testing, documentation, and maintainability standards.

Lead or contribute to cross-functional initiatives spanning data science, software engineering, and laboratory teams, ensuring delivery of fit-for-purpose solutions.

Promote the adoption and effective use of in-house tools, applications, and data science methods to maximize impact across Translational Medicine and PKS.

Stay current with advances in AI/ML, statistics, and computational methods relevant to ADME, PK/PD, and drug discovery, and help bring appropriate innovation into practice.

Essential Requirements

Advanced degree in a relevant scientific or quantitative field such as cheminformatics, bioinformatics, biomedical engineering, computational biology, computational chemistry, data science, AI/ML in life sciences, or a related discipline.

PhD with 5+ years or MSc with 8+ years of relevant work experience applying data science in drug discovery, translational research, or related scientific environments.

Strong expertise in machine learning, statistics, and reproducible data science workflows, with demonstrated ability to apply them to real scientific problems.

Proficiency in Python and/or R, with solid software development practices including version control, testing, documentation, and production-quality coding standards.

Experience designing, developing, and deploying robust analytical applications, computational workflows, or machine learning systems in collaborative environments.

Demonstrated ability to work across multidisciplinary teams and translate complex analytical concepts into clear, actionable insights for scientists and stakeholders.

Strong communication, collaboration, and leadership capabilities, with the ability to influence decisions in cross-functional settings.

Good understanding of drug discovery processes, with particular relevance to ADME, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, or related translational data domains.

Desirable Requirements

Experience with discovery-stage PK modeling, ADME data interpretation, or relating preclinical properties to in vivo pharmacokinetic behavior.

Familiarity with modern machine learning approaches such as deep learning, generative algorithms, or explainable AI in drug discovery contexts.

Experience with modern scientific software or web application development frameworks, including JavaScript-based front-end technologies (e.g., Svelte).

Knowledge of SQL, databases, Linux-based environments, and scalable data engineering patterns for scientific workflows.

Experience working with small molecules, peptides, RNAs, or other modalities in discovery-stage data analysis.

In this role, you manage the preparation, coordination and follow-up of interventions, working closely with engineers, technicians, consultants and contractors to ensure safe and compliant operations. You will join the Civil Engineering section (CE) within the Site Asset Management (SAM) Group.
Functions
Act as the referent for pollutant-related works within the SCE-SAM group, managing the of hazardous materials decontamination activities at CERN.
Act as contract manager for hazardous substances decontamination frame contracts, overseeing budget, quality, schedule and safety, and managing financial variations, claims and settlements with contractors.
Serve as the referent of the civil engineering section for works and projects in technical galleries and the Proton Synchrotron complex facility.
Manage project design steps (preliminary, concept design, developed project design, building permit, technical specifications and relevant documentation for tenders and execution design) in collaboration with internal CERN entities as well as the consultants and contractors appointed.
Plan and manage the execution of construction and renovation projects, including coordination of various trades, utilisation of service and frame contracts and contract management, chairing site and coordination meetings, and monitoring cost, quality, schedule and safety until final acceptance.
