This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position

A healthier future. It’s what drives us to innovate. To continuously advance science and ensure everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for generations to come. Creating a world where we all have more time with the people we love. That’s what makes us Roche.

In this Leadership position in Pharma Technical Regulatory (PTR) you will have a broad understanding of the regulatory landscape and apply your knowledge in the execution of deliverables aligned with our North Star. As a leader you are accountable for advocating and driving changes throughout the organization and supporting our people in an agile environment. You will have a thorough understanding of priorities and areas of high impact, connect the right people and resources with the right work and help the organization adapt to evolving regulatory requirements. You will inspire all of our people to boldly innovate, collaborate and create outcomes that matter for patients, stakeholders and the company.
In the role of a Group Director you will oversee both Portfolio Leadership and People Leadership supporting / enabling teams and people within this operating model (PTR ecosystem) to deliver on overall business objectives.

The Opportunity

You will have oversight and full accountability for the development and implementation of end-to-end regulatory strategies and initiatives on a portfolio level.

You will define long-term vision and strategies across product portfolios and cross-functional initiatives (targeting innovation, operational excellence, and policy), ensuring transparency across squads and teams.

You will enable self-managed teams by serving as a visionary, architect, coach, and catalyst to the organization, taking responsibility for performance management, objective feedback, and regular development discussions.

You will work collaboratively at the global level with other leaders to align on priorities, drive resource planning and budgeting, and support strategic projects as needed.

You will stay abreast of internal and external developments and trends to maintain a current perspective of implications for all programs, driving internal and external awareness.

You will lead health authority interactions and submission reviews for assigned projects with an expanded scope, representing Technical Regulatory at multidisciplinary meetings.

You will be a key point of contact for one (or more) regulatory capability area(s) (e.g., CTA, NDA, LCM, data management, systems) to drive operational efficiency and excellence.

You will serve as the voice of the organization, build and maintain relationships with key internal stakeholders, and communicate challenges, opportunities, and initiatives to employees in a systematic manner.

You will anticipate and remove organizational barriers that impede forward action and progress.

Who You Are
You are a visionary, adaptable, and strategic leader who thrives in an agile, global ecosystem. You bring exceptional negotiation skills, foster a culture of continuous coaching and growth, and excel at translating complex regulatory landscapes into clear action while empowering self-managed teams to innovate boldly for patients.
Furthermore, you possess the following qualifications and experience:

Master’s or Post Graduate Degree in life sciences

15 or more years of work experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry, with significant global CMC regulatory leadership experience across the full product life-cycle.

Deep expertise in global CMC regulatory landscapes, hands-on experience in scenario planning, balanced regulatory risk assessment, and a proven track record representing the company in health authority interactions and influencing regulatory science.

Strong technical understanding of drug substance & drug product manufacturing and analytics in Small and/or Large Molecules, alongside a solid grasp of drug development, commercialization processes, supply chain complexity, and Pharmaceutical Quality Systems.

Proven track record of direct people management and cross-functional, global team leadership, with excellent communication and presentation skills to synthesize complex issues and expedite executive decision-making.

Strategic perspective on Regulatory Information Management systems and digital tools to drive compliance, efficiency, and excellence across the regulatory ecosystem.

This role requires travel up to 10%.

Are you ready to lead, innovate, and make a meaningful difference for our patients? We are looking forward to your application – join us now and become part of our journey!
 
 

Who we are
A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Introduction:
As a Structural Civil Engineer, you will be responsible for the design, analysis and technical oversight of civil engineering structures throughout the project lifecycle, from feasibility studies to construction support. Au sein de l’équipe informatique du Département de médecine, vous êtes le garant ou la garante de bonne utilisation et du bon fonctionnement des systèmes informatiques propres au département. Vous êtes également l’interlocuteur ou l'interlocutrice privilégiée qui garantit à la DTN-IA la transmission des informations sur les logiciels transversaux mais également dans les interfaçages aux logiciels du département.
Vous dirigez l’équipe informatique du département de médecine composée de 5 personnes qui travaillent selon leurs compétences en tant qu’informaticiens, concepteur de formulaires dans DPI et data manager.
Vous assurez le respect des directives institutionnelles dans le périmètre de l’informatique en collaborant étroitement avec la DTN-IA, le Service biomédical et équipements, la Direction de l’immobilier, la centrale d’achat, vous collaborez activement avec les fournisseurs, vous gérez certains projets dans leur totalité.
L’équipe informatique gère environ quatre-vingts logiciels propres au département. Il s’agit de garantir leur installation, leur migration, leur conformité avec la sécurité informatique des HUG, leur bonne utilisation par les collaborateurs, leur potentiel interfaçage avec les autres logiciels de l’institution.
Le département de médecine c’est 1'300 collaboratrices et collaborateurs avec des besoins en équipements informatiques (ordinateurs, imprimantes, accessoires …) et en téléphonie (téléphone, abonnements …). Vous évaluez le besoin en tenant compte de l’économicité demandée.
L’équipe informatique du département gère aussi la mise en production de nouveau formulaire générique pour la documentation clinique dans l’application informatique DPI (Dossier Patient Informatisé), ainsi que les modifications de ces derniers.
Vous participez à de nombreux projets d’amélioration continue.
Vous participez aux instances permanentes de la DTN-IA et à des commissions ou des groupes de projets institutionnels.
Vous assurez également la coordination informatique dans des projets architecturaux du département.

Le bureau de facturation assure le traitement des dossiers pour 4 départements : le Département de médecine (D-MED), le Département de médecine communautaire et de premier recours (D-MCPR), le Département d’oncologie (D-ONCO), et le Département de médecine Aigue (D-MA).
Au sein de l’équipe du Centre d’admission et de facturation du Département de médecine (CAF), vous assurez le traitement des factures de prestations ambulatoires en réclamation, des différentes listes de rejets, de la réponse téléphonique aux différentes demandes, de l’accueil des patients et patientes pour le règlement des factures immédiates et de toutes autres missions en rapport avec votre fonction.
Vous vous inscrivez dans une dynamique de continuité de service en prenant le relai de vos collègues en cas d’absence et en favorisant l’échange d’informations au sein de l’équipe. Vous n’hésitez pas à vous perfectionner dans vos activités en sollicitant l’aide adéquate. Plus généralement, vous contribuez à toutes activités visant à améliorer la qualité des prestations.

Au sein du Service talents et leadership et suite à une évolution interne, vous rejoignez une équipe de 7 personnes en charge des activités de recrutement transversales. Dans cette équipe en pleine évolution, vous avez diverses responsabilités en lien avec l’attractivité et le recrutement, et vous contribuez au développement des axes de la feuille de route RH.  
Vous apportez un support complet aux cinq spécialistes RH en recrutement pour tous les mandats de recrutement sous leur responsabilité. Durant la phase de pré-sélection, vous assurez l’analyse qualitative des candidatures reçues pour des campagnes transversales et volumiques ainsi que sur des mandats plus spécifiques. Vous suivez les différentes étapes du processus de recrutement, incluant la planification des entretiens, la gestion des mises en situation, et la réponse aux candidatures. En parallèle, vous assurez une réponse à l’ensemble des candidatures spontanées reçues sous format papier ou mail. 
De plus, vous gérez l’ensemble du processus des remplacements d’été représentant plus de 1'000 candidatures durant la période estivale. Dans votre rôle, vous assurez la publication de l’annonce, l’évaluation et l’orientation des candidatures, puis la gestion contractuelle de l’ensemble des personnes recrutées jusqu’à la rédaction des attestations de travail. Vous supervisez ponctuellement une équipe de 4 personnes dédiées à ce processus. 
Vous participez à l’organisation d’événements dédiés au recrutement tels que les campagnes de recrutement, les mises en situation et les salons professionnels et contribuez régulièrement aux projets du service.  
De manière périodique, vous établissez des indicateurs relatifs à votre activité. Vous êtes à l’aise avec l’utilisation courante d’Excel pour des tableaux dynamiques croisés, des tableaux de suivi, publipostage etc. 
Vous faites preuve d’un excellent sens du service auprès des clients internes et maintenez un contact de qualité avec les candidates et candidats, les managers et les équipes RH en identifiant des solutions répondant aux besoins tout en vous assurant du respect de la politique de recrutement institutionnelle et des bonnes pratiques. 
En soutien à votre collègue Assistante en recrutement, vous êtes une personne de contact pour les équipes RH, vous gérez les demandes de plus de 1000 publications d’annonces à l'année, provenant des départements et des directions. Vous garantissez leur publication avec une qualité rédactionnelle favorisant l’attractivité et la conformité avec les pratiques institutionnelles. Vous conseillez également les équipes internes sur la rédaction des annonces. La gestion des différents canaux de recrutement utilisés aux HUG (JobBoards, LinkedIn, presse spécialisée) fait partie de vos responsabilités en suppléance. A ce titre, vous analysez les demandes spécifiques de publications et vous entreprenez les démarches associées. 
En binôme, vous apportez du support aux utilisateurs et utilisatrices de l’ATS SmartRecruiters, vous pouvez assurer la formation de prise en main de la plate-forme et fournissez assistance aux membres des services RH, en résolvant les problèmes pour assurer une utilisation optimale de l’outil. 
Nous offrons un environnement collaboratif et stimulant, une équipe active, la participation à des projets RH ambitieux.

Intégrez et renforcez une équipe composée de 2 développeurs fullstack et un lead développeur, dont la mission est de poursuivre le développement et l’évolution de l’application Greco, le logiciel de gestion de planning et de téléconsultation utilisé par le personnel. Le logiciel est également utilisé par les patients et patientes grâce à l’application Concerto. L’équipe travaille de manière agile en s’inspirant fortement de la méthodologie Scrum tout en s’adaptant aux contraintes liées au milieu hospitalier qui impliquent d’être capable de parfois devoir changer rapidement de tâche pour s’adapter aux priorités. 
Vous participez à la rédaction des cahiers des charges techniques, en traduisant les besoins fonctionnels en spécifications détaillées. À partir des spécifications techniques, vous développez le logiciel, aussi bien sur la partie front-end que back-end, en utilisant les technologies de pointe et une architecture microservices. Vous faites évoluer la solution et garantissez sa maintenance, tout en assurant un suivi rigoureux. Concrètement, vous développez en autonomie les fonctionnalités et corrections qui vous sont attribuées. 
Grâce à votre esprit d’équipe, vous collaborez étroitement avec l’équipe pour développer des solutions et des fonctionnalités fiables et évolutives.  Vous partagez les meilleures pratiques et adoptez une approche critique et constructive dans une optique d’amélioration continue en faisant preuve d’une forte orientation solution. 
Tout au long du cycle de vie du produit, grâce à votre sens de la communication, vous contribuez au développement du logiciel de manière optimale et structurée, assurant un lien essentiel avec les coordinateurs et coordinatrices greco des différents départements médicaux. Vous adaptez votre langage en fonction de vos interlocuteurs et interlocutrices pour vulgariser les termes techniques, challengez les solutions proposées, et collaborez activement avec les parties prenantes pour trouver les adaptations les plus pertinentes. 
De plus, vous veillez à la mise à jour et à la rédaction de la documentation nécessaire. Vous mettez à profit votre capacité de synthèse et votre pragmatisme pour mener votre mission dans les délais impartis et garantir un résultat de qualité. 
Vous participez activement à l’ensemble des phases d'un projet informatique, de son initialisation à sa finalisation, en vous assurant de produire les livrables attendus à chacune de ces phases. En outre, vous assurez également le support utilisateurs de niveau 3, en relation avec les autres services de la DTN-IA, tout en assurant une orientation client forte.

The Position
 In Roche’s Pharmaceutical Research and Early Development organisation (pRED), we make transformative medicines for patients in order to tackle some of the world’s toughest unmet healthcare needs. At pRED, we are united by our mission to transform science into medicines. Together, we create a culture defined by curiosity, responsibility, and humility, where our talented people are empowered and inspired to bring forward extraordinary life-changing innovation at speed.

pRED Cardiovascular, Metabolism, Immunology (CMI), located in Basel, Switzerland, focuses on the discovery and early development of innovative treatments for specific diseases that affect the lives of millions. In the Immunology Department, we are developing cutting-edge therapies to treat chronic inflammatory diseases, including novel treatment options for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). 

The Opportunity

To complement the Immunology team in pRED CMI, we are seeking a visionary, highly motivated, experienced Scientist with a strong academic background in pulmonary research, a track record in drug target identification and validation and proven ability to effectively lead projects in a drug discovery setting.

As a Principal Scientist in pRED CMI, you will be a part of an international and multidisciplinary group of scientists and clinicians committed to delivering innovative solutions for COPD patients by combining cutting-edge approaches in biology, pharmacology and translational research. 

Key Responsibilities:

Utilising patient data and translational models, you will lead innovative initiatives to gain a better understanding of COPD pathobiology in order to identify novel drug targets and generate therapeutic hypotheses that are experimentally testable, druggable and clinically developable.

In collaboration with a dedicated team of lab-based associates and post-doctoral scientists, you will direct, oversee and interpret complex preclinical experimental studies for the validation and characterisation of targets or therapeutic agents in COPD.

You will bring targets into the early drug discovery pipeline and lead multidisciplinary teams up to clinical candidate generation.

Working in multidisciplinary teams, you will diligently evaluate external opportunities and clearly communicate the findings to senior management 

People management, including coaching and mentoring junior scientists and postdocs 

Who You Are

You hold a PhD degree in Life Sciences (respiratory biology, cellular/ molecular biology, pharmacology, immunology - or a closely related field) and bring 5 to 10 years of experience in the pharmaceutical industry. 
You bring deep expertise in COPD disease biology, including chronic tissue remodelling, inflammation and/ or epithelial biology 
You have significant scientific accomplishments and successful collaborations documented by publications in high-impact journals
You have a strong strategic thinking capacity, with the ability to balance multiple priorities in a fast-paced, matrixed organisation. 
You have a good understanding of general pharmacological properties of therapeutic modalities such as small molecules and antibodies. 
You can effectively communicate scientific data and concepts to colleagues, teams and senior management. 

At Roche, we aim high to deliver life-changing healthcare solutions. If you’re ready to make a meaningful impact on patients and healthcare systems worldwide, this is the place for you.  
 
 

Who we are
A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.

Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Therapeutic Modalities (TMo) organization, accountable for translating disease biology into high-quality drug candidates across small molecules, large molecules, oligonucleotides, and genomic medicines. The Opportunity

Joining Small Molecule Research Discovery within Therapeutic Modalities, you will work within a highly engaged, cross-functional team bridging cell biology, automation, and multiple therapeutic areas. In this role, you drive innovation through strong commitment to lab science by developing the foundational cellular models that power our drug discovery pipeline.

Imaging & Screening: Solid exposure to high-content imaging, assay development, automated cell culture, or high-throughput screening using small molecules or genetic tools. Expertise in high-content data analysis, image processing pipelines, or multiparametric data evaluation is a  plus. 

Communication & Mindset: Resourceful, flexible problem-solving skills with a highly collaborative approach and strong communication skills in English.

Job Description Summary#LI-Hybrid
Internal Title: Senior Principal Scientist or Associate Director
Location: Basel, Switzerland

The Modeling & Simulation group within PK Sciences is looking for a Principal Scientist to Associate Director level modeler, to develop and apply translational physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling along with data analysis techniques to facilitate drug discovery, development, and translational research across disease areas. Importantly, the candidate has experience with regulatory submissions and in successful regulatory interactions. The candidate’s core responsibilities will include PBPK modeling to integrate in vitro and in vivo data for drug-drug interaction (DDI) assessments, impact of biopharmaceutics properties on absorption, and pharmacokinetic (PK) predictions in humans as well as in specific populations (e.g. disease, organ impairment, pediatrics). The ultimate goal of this work is to be on the forefront of applying PBPK models to inform the safe administration of our drug candidates in the clinic, to optimize clinical trial designs, and waive clinical trials, ultimately, to get our medicines to patients faster.

The role requires a deep understanding of ADME/DMPK principles and biopharmaceutics knowledge, experience with industry standard PBPK modeling packages (such as GastroPlus or Simcyp) or bespoke PBPK models, regulatory submissions involving PBPK modeling, interdisciplinary thinking and great attention to detail. The applicant will work in a dynamic and multidisciplinary environment to build, verify and apply quality translational/biopharmaceutical PBPK models.

 
Job Description
Key responsibilities:

Expert PBPK modeler to provide translational modeling support for global drug discovery and development projects

Perform translational PBPK analyses to predict clinical drug exposure in specific populations, assess potential for DDI, understand clinical impact of disease on drug exposure, as well as apply biopharmaceutic PBPK modeling to support formulation changes and achieve clinical biowaivers

Integrate PK/ PD data, ADME and DDI findings

Ability to interpret and communicate modeling results and potential impact to project teams

Prepare summary documents for use in regulatory submissions and ability to respond independently to health authority questions

Essential requirements

PhD in pharmaceutical sciences or related discipline with experience in ADME/DMPK sciences, biopharmaceutics, and modeling and simulation. At least 5+ years in pharmaceutical industry including demonstrated knowledge and experience with PBPK modeling.  The level of the position would depend upon the experience of the candidate.

Hands on experience with PBPK modeling tools such as PK-Sim, Simcyp, or GastroPlus is required.  In addition, experience with modeling software such as Monolix, R, Phoenix, or Nonmem is desired. 

Experience in authoring regulatory documents, knowledge of global regulatory requirements and guidance

Broad knowledge of drug discovery and development, e.g., pharmacokinetics, drug delivery, formulation, ADME, DDI, etc.

This is a hybrid role that requires a balance of in-person and virtual working, with an average of 12 days a month on site in Basel, Switzerland.
Candidates with demonstrated impact as a modeler, preferably in the pharmaceutical/biotech industry, and with commensurate experience and proficiency may be considered for the Principal Scientist II (5+ years) or Associate Director (8+ years) role.

Introduction:
You will join CERN's Polymer Laboratory within the Superconducting Magnet Technology section to develop and qualify advanced polymer and composite materials.
You will contribute to the design, validation and implementation of innovative materials, used in CERN accelerator systems within a cryogenic, high-voltage and radiation environment.
Functions:
Develop and qualify novel polymer and composite materials for superconducting magnets and accelerator technologies, with particular emphasis on cryogenic operation, high-voltage insulation and radiation resistance.
Design and validate manufacturing and processing techniques for superconducting magnet insulation systems, including resin transfer processes, bonding technologies, composite fabrication and additive manufacturing.
Lead research and design projects within the Polymer Laboratory to address the evolving needs of CERN accelerator complex and experimental facilities.
Contribute to the laboratory developments by identifying material technologies and processing techniques and establishing new experimental capabilities.

The Geodetic Metrology Group (BE-GM) provides metrology and alignment for accelerator components, beam lines, and experiments across CERN, including geodetic reference systems and gravity field modelling. The Future Projects section prepares technical foundations for upcoming facilities through studies, simulations, and prototyping.
In this role, you will contribute to FCC studies, developing gravity field models for the 91 km tunnel and supporting sub-millimetric alignment of accelerator components and detectors. You will also contribute to the CERN-Swisstopo collaboration to compute the quasi-geoid model required for Switzerland's New Height System.
Your responsibilities:
Compute and validate a state-of-the-art quasi-geoid model covering FCC area and Switzerland.
Explore and propose solutions for modelling equipotential surfaces inside tunnels.
Take part in field observation campaigns (gravity, GNSS, leveling, astro-geodetic) required to fill data gaps or to validate the computed models.
Develop a gravity field modelling software package by combining existing tools and new features developed for the project.
This role includes team supervision responsibilities.
Your profile:
Knowledge of physical geodesy and gravity field theory.
Experience in regional gravity field modelling using GRAVSOFT, GROOPS, KTH, SHGEO or another method would be an asset.
Experience in object-oriented programming (ideally Python and/or C++).
Skills:
Good organisation and communication skills, sense of responsibility and a capacity to work in a team.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the basics of the other language.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
You have a professional background in Topography, Geodesy, Surveying, Geomatic (or a related field) and have either:
a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;
or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

Vous intégrez une unité de soins intermédiaires de 14 lits. Cette unité accueille des patients et patientes relevant des spécialités de neurologie vasculaire, de neurochirurgie et de neurologie générale.  
Vous dispensez, de manière autonome et sur délégation médicale, des soins infirmiers personnalisés avec une surveillance rapprochée à une patientèle de tout âge.
Vous évoluez dans un contexte de soins aigus qui nécessite l’utilisation de dispositifs médicaux et d'appareils médico-techniques.
Vous savez analyser les situations cliniques complexes et avez une aptitude à gérer les imprévus grâce aux différents monitorings.
Vous êtes une personne engagée dans la qualité des soins et vous orientez vos prises en soins garantissant des soins sécuritaires.
Vous faites preuve d’excellentes compétences relationnelles et considérez le ou la patiente ainsi que ses proches comme partenaire de la prise en charge.
Vous participez à l'encadrement et à l'enseignement clinique du nouveau personnel soignant et d'autres professionnelles et professionnels de la santé. Vous assurez avec précision et rigueur la transmission d’informations en interprofessionnalité.
Vos capacités d'apprentissage vous permettent de progresser en permanence dans votre pratique.

Dans le cadre de ce mandat, vous assurez la prise en charge nutritionnelle des patients et patientes adultes en poly-oncologie selon le processus de soins nutritionnels.
Vous réalisez régulièrement des mesures de calorimétrie indirecte et de composition corporelle, participez activement aux différents colloques cliniques et fonctionnels et veillez au maintien de l'harmonisation des prises en charge nutritionnelles en appliquant les principes de l'Evidence Based Medicine ainsi que les recommandations des sociétés expertes.
Vous contribuez activement à la prévention de la malnutrition protéino-énergétique en lien avec les pathologies et les traitements, animez des ateliers et des cours destinés aux différents professionnels de la santé et collaborez avec l'équipe multidisciplinaire spécialisée.
Vous contribuez au maintien d'une dynamique d'équipe constructive et collaborative et assurez, au besoin, le remplacement de vos collègues sur le secteur de l'oncologie ainsi que dans les autres unités de soins aigus.

Vous participez à la prise en soins des patients et patientes au sein d’une unité de médecine et néphrologie en assurant des soins d’hygiène et de confort.
Sous la responsabilité de l'infirmier ou infirmière, vous préparez et distribuez des traitements à la patientèle et transmettez et documentez toutes les informations nécessaires à la prise en soins des patients et patientes dans le dossier patient.
Vous prodiguez des soins et effectuez des actes médicotechniques relevant de la compétence des ASSC et participez à appliquer des mesures de promotion de la santé et prévention de la maladie.
Vous soutenez et suppléez de manière autonome et responsable, la patientèle dans les activités de la vie quotidienne. 
Vous participez à la gestion des commandes, des stocks de médicaments et des biens de consommation.
Vous travaillez avec les applications informatiques notamment DPI et Winrest.

Dans le cadre de votre mission, vous accueillez et renseignez toutes les personnes se présentant à la réception des Bains de Cressy (patientèle et clientèle hétéroclite).
Vous avez la tâche d'encaisser les entrées, les abonnements et toutes autres prestations (numéraires, cartes de crédit, bons cadeaux).
Vous assurez la permanence téléphonique ainsi que la prise de rendez-vous des prestataires externes tels que les esthéticiens et esthéticiennes, masseurs et masseuses, etc et vous mettez en place les cabines de soins de bien-être.
Vous conseillez, promouvez et vendez les différentes prestations des Bains de Cressy et effectuez divers travaux administratifs (comptabilité et facturation, production de statistiques, gestion du système de parking, gestion du stock et de l’e-boutique).
Vous avez une grande résistance au stress, une excellente capacité de concentration et à faire face aux imprévus ainsi qu'une polyvalence avérée pour un poste multi-tâches.
Vous êtes capable de désamorcer des situations complexes et/ou conflictuelles avec une clientèle hétéroclite.

Dans le cadre d’un remplacement à durée déterminée de 7 mois, vous êtes rattachée ou rattaché directement au chef de département, vous organisez les rendez-vous et les séances en gérant son agenda. Vous rédigez les comptes-rendus des diverses séances départementales et coordonnez le suivi des décisions prises. Vous travaillez avec un fort degré d’autonomie, tout en sachant collaborer avec les interlocuteurs internes et externes aux HUG.
Vous menez à bien les activités administratives en lien avec votre fonction telles que la gestion des horaires (VRH) de médecins et secrétaires et appuyez le médecin cadre en charge de l’organisation des gardes hospitalières dans cette tâche.
Vous participez aussi au processus de recrutement des nouveaux médecins internes et organisez les séances de la Commission de la filière du département.

En tant qu’infirmier ou infirmière spécialisée en soins intensifs de néonatologie et pédiatriques, vous dispensez de manière autonome et/ou sur délégation médicale, des soins infirmiers spécialisés et globaux à tout nouveau-né, enfant ou adolescent ou adolescente et dans des situations présentant différents niveaux de complexité.
Vous intégrez les parents dans la prise en soins de leur enfant et les considérez comme des partenaires avec un accompagnement adapté. Travailler avec des enfants prématurés en soutenant les parents dans ce moment de vie particulier sera votre quotidien.
Vous travaillez dans les unités de soins intensifs de néonatologie et pédiatriques et collaborez activement à l’encadrement et l’enseignement du nouveau personnel soignant, des étudiantes ou étudiants et d’autres professionnelles ou professionnels de la santé. 
Grâce à votre professionnalisme, vous contribuez au développement de la qualité des soins et à la recherche dans le domaine de la santé.

The actual location of this job is in Basel Stücki, Switzerland.

For Drug Product Services (DPS), our successful DP focused branch located in Basel and Stein, Switzerland, we have exciting opportunities. Become part of a group that enables its customers to meet some of the greatest challenges in patient treatment and join us by applying for the Associate Principal Scientist E&L position.

What you will get:

An agile career and a dynamic work culture

An inclusive and ethical workplace

Compensation programs that recognize high performance

Perform and supervise Extractables & Leachables (EL) laboratory studies (HS-GC-MS, GC-MS, LC-UV-MS) to support DPS projects, as well as perform services for external customers

Perform and supervise EL assessments according to Lonza internal procedures and best scientific practices

Supervise lab scientists and interns. Ensure effective use of resources (time, people, equipment and materials). Review and approve data, and compile protocols, reports and SOPs

Enable innovation and technical strategy projects, generate intellectual property, as well as evaluate and implement new technologies as required

Closely interact with the other functions across Forensic Chemistry, DPS and the wider Lonza network

Substantial work experience and background in hyphenated analytical methodologies

Ready to shape the future of life sciences? Apply now.

Introduction:
You will play an active role in the support and evolution of the database systems that underpin the LHC experiments, accelerator operations, and CERN's support services. In addition to general database administration, you will focus on the engineering, operation, and modernisation of orchestrated High Availability (HA) infrastructures. A key responsibility will be the development and operation of a resilient, distributed PostgreSQL HA platform based on modern consensus, orchestration, and proxy routing technologies.
A hands-on engineering role focused on the reliability, automation and evolution of CERN’s PostgreSQL and relational database platforms, with a particular focus on high availability, resilience and service continuity for mission-critical scientific and organisational services.
Functions:
As a Database Infrastructure Engineer in the Databases and Analytics Group, your main activities will consist of:
Administration, operation, and evolution of MySQL, and PostgreSQL database platforms, including troubleshooting, configuration, migrations, upgrades, scaling, and patching.
Design, deployment, operation, and continuous improvement of highly available and resilient PostgreSQL infrastructures.
Development and maintenance of automation for database provisioning, configuration, failover and operational workflows.
Proactive monitoring of database environments to ensure optimum performance, throughput, stability, availability and security.
Definition and evolution of database architecture, resilience, disaster recovery, and service continuity strategies.
Provision of technical expertise and troubleshooting support to application development teams.
Share domain and technical expertise, and provide technical mentorship and training to peers.

Introduction
Join the Deployment and Operations team in the Communication Systems and  Fabric Group and contribute to the reliable connectivity that supports one of the world’s leading scientific research environments. You will coordinate and follow up telecom and network infrastructure works across CERN sites, working with contractors, users and technical teams to plan installations, check quality, ensure safety and maintain accurate documentation. We welcome candidates with hands-on experience in cabling, telecom, electrical, industrial infrastructure or network installation environments who are motivated to develop in a unique international setting.
Functions
Review cabling requests and collaborate with requesters to clarify needs when necessary.
Help define suitable cable types and routes, working with users and taking into account the local environment.
Coordinate cabling and de-cabling activities with both internal teams and external partners (e.g. contractors).
Prepare clear and practical documentation to support the work (such as drawings and technical plans).
Contribute to safe working practices by identifying potential risks and supporting the implementation of mitigation measures in line with CERN standards.
Support the organisation of logistics for cabling activities, including materials, access, and required equipment.
Participate in worksite coordination and follow-up meetings.
Track progress and help ensure that work is carried out safely and with good quality.
Take part in inspections and acceptance of completed work, and help keep infrastructure records up to date.

The Senior Medical Materials Coordinator provides medical, scientific and regulatory support for Switzerland and serves as the legally required person responsible for advertising in accordance with Art. 25 AWV (Arzneimittel-Werbeverordnung). The role ensures that promotional and non-promotional materials are scientifically accurate, balanced and aligned with Swiss regulatory requirements.
Aligned with regional objectives and the Global Medical Plan, the Senior Medical Materials Coordinator supports local medical and promotional initiatives and scientific projects by applying medical and scientific expertise to the review and communication of clinical data and scientific evidence. The position contributes to local medical activities while providing high-quality medical and scientific guidance across the organisation.
Working closely with cross-functional teams, the role supports the review and approval of medical and promotional materials and helps ensure the appropriate use of scientific information in internal and external communications.
Key Responsibilities/Scope of the Job:
Act as the officially designated Person Responsible for Advertising in accordance with Art. 25 AWV.
Provides support for KVV Art. 71a–d reimbursement requests
Review and approve promotional and non-promotional materials to ensure scientific accuracy, balance and alignment with Swiss regulatory requirements.
Maintain the legally required archive of promotional materials and serve as the primary contact for Swissmedic regarding advertising-related matters.
Apply medical and scientific expertise to evaluate and communicate clinical data and scientific evidence.
Monitor relevant scientific developments, clinical publications and treatment trends to support informed medical decision-making.
Provide medical and scientific guidance to internal stakeholders and contribute to training activities where appropriate.
Support local non-promotional and promotional initiatives, scientific communications and medical education activities in alignment with regional and global objectives.
Contribute to the development and review of medical and promotional content and ensure the consistent use of scientific information across internal and external communications.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to provide high-quality medical and scientific support across the organisation.

What you'll do:
You will spend up to 36 months working on your doctoral thesis in a truly unique environment where science, technology and innovation meet. You’ll be part of an international community of experts, gaining experience at the forefront of research and engineering.
Your responsibilities:
Carry out your doctoral research in collaboration with CERN and your home university.
Contribute to ongoing projects in domains such as applied physics, computing, engineering or related technical fields.
Present and document your work as part of your academic and research objectives.
Learn from and work alongside world-class scientists, engineers and technicians within an international and multidisciplinary team.
Your profile:
Your field of study is in Applied Physics, Engineering, Computing, or a related area.
You are motivated to develop your research in a hands-on, collaborative and innovative environment.
You enjoy teamwork and learning from others in a collaborative setting.
Your skills:
Solid theoretical foundation in your research area, combined with an interest in practical applications.
Curiosity, precision and a proactive attitude towards learning.
Good communication skills and ability to work effectively in a multicultural team.

We are seeking a motivated and proactive Safety Support Specialist to contribute to the coordination and execution of safety activities during a major infrastructure and upgrade programme at CERN.
Working alongside project managers, safety officers and technical experts, you will help ensure the safe implementation of upgrade, consolidation, maintenance, dismantling and commissioning activities across a wide range of accelerator facilities to enable future scientific operations. The job will have two main focus points: project management and project safety.
Your responsibilities
Support the coordination of schedules, resources, documentation, and stakeholder communications.
Follow-up on safety-related activities, ensuring alignment between technical, operational, and safety stakeholders.
Assist with planning, implementation, and monitoring of safety measures.
Prepare, review, and update safety documentation, including contributions to the Safety File for new and existing facilities.
Track project actions, maintain records, and support progress reporting and follow-up activities.
Participate in project meetings, site visits, and technical reviews.
Contribute to safety review and risk assessments related to chemical, nano, electrical and radiological hazards.
Support operation readiness activities to facilitate the safe execution and commissioning of upgraded facilities and systems.
Contribute to the implementation and monitoring of safety controls.
Assist with on-site follow-up (above and underground) and contractor coordination as needed.
Your profile
Initial experience through e.g. internships, research projects or academic work with:
Project execution and coordination activities.
Preparation of technical and safety documentation.
Worksite risk assessment and management.
Installation, testing, commissioning, or operational readiness activities.
Work in complex technical environments and safety-critical facilities.
Skills
Basic understanding of chemical, electrical and radiological safety principles and standards; willingness to further develop expertise in these areas.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teams and stakeholders.
Proactive, organised, and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and work both independently and as part of a team.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a keen interest in safety, engineering, and project delivery.
Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the other language.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Electrical Engineering, Safety Engineering, Chemical Engineering (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is either a Bachelor's or Master's degree.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.
Applicants without University degree are not eligible.
Applicants with a PhD are not eligible.

Are you passionate about data, problem-solving, and turning complex information into clear insights? Do you enjoy maintaining and improving data systems, from legacy databases to modern reporting platforms? Join our agile, self-organised team of engineers to help maintain and develop CERN's Corporate Information Systems! Take Part!  You'll be part of the Business Computing (BC) group, supporting Finance and Procurement.
Your mission: analyse, improve, and help modernise reporting and data solutions, while supporting the transformation of CERN's enterprise systems and ensuring that future analytics needs are properly understood and addressed.
Your responsibilities:
Extract, transform, model, and visualise data in reports, dashboards, and analytics platforms;
Interact with relational databases, mainly Oracle, using SQL and PL/SQL;
Develop, maintain, and test reporting data models and semantic models supporting CERN's Finance and Procurement systems;
Maintain, support, and enhance existing reporting and data solutions while helping define and implement their future evolution;
Contribute to data profiling, mapping, quality checks, validation, and reconciliation activities during migration and transition phases;
Contribute to the development and maintenance of ETL/ELT pipelines and other data-processing activities where required;
Collaborate with business users, functional experts, architects, and developers to ensure data consistency, usability, and technical feasibility;
Support testing, troubleshooting, documentation, maintenance, and third-level support for reporting and data solutions.
Your profile:
Data Analysis & Reporting:
Experience in SQL (writing, optimising, debugging complex queries).
Familiarity with data visualisation or analytics tools such as Power BI, R, or Python-based dashboards.
Understanding of data modelling principles (dimensional/star schema design, semantic models, data warehouses).
Experience analysing data structures, flows, and dependencies in complex enterprise systems.
Data Engineering:
Exposure to data pipeline concepts and tools such as SQL, dbt, Airflow, or Python for data processing.
Interest in maintaining and modernising reporting and data solutions during a systems transformation.
Business Processes & User Support:
Interest in providing end-user support, troubleshooting, escalation, and issue resolution.
Awareness of Finance and Procurement processes or interest in learning about business domains.
Collaboration:
Experience working in group projects, ideally in collaborative or Agile environments.
Skills:
Data & Analytics:
Excellent knowledge of SQL and relational databases.
Knowledge of data visualisation and analytics tools, particularly Power BI.
Ability to contribute to the design and maintenance of data models for reporting and analytics.
Ability to understand and document complex data structures, data flows, dependencies, and transformation logic.
Data Governance & Quality:
Awareness of data quality, security, and governance concepts.
Attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.
Technical Environment:
Knowledge of version control systems and basic interaction with Linux servers via the command line.
Knowledge of Agile practices and experience maintaining reporting solutions and data pipelines in an agile environment.
Comfortable in working with both new and legacy systems.
Communication & Collaboration:
Excellent communication skills and the ability to present complex information effectively.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Computer Science (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is either a Bachelor's or Master's degree.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.
Applicants without University degree are not eligible.
Applicants with a PhD are not eligible.

Introduction
As Business Continuity Lead, you will play a central role in strengthening CERN’s organisational resilience by leading and coordinating business continuity activities across the Organization.
Working in the Improvement, Continuity and Sustainability (OSI-ICS) Group within the Organisational Support and Improvement (OSI) Department, you will contribute to the consolidation of CERN’s approach to risk management, crisis preparedness and business continuity within an integrated governance framework.
Functions
Develop, implement and maintain CERN’s Business Continuity Management (BCM) framework, in alignment with CERN policies, international standards and good practice.
Facilitate and coordinate the identification and analysis of critical activities, dependencies, vulnerabilities and recovery requirements together with process and service owners.
Coordinate and support the development of Business Continuity Plans (BCPs) and disaster recovery arrangements across departments and functions.
Contribute to the integration of business continuity management with CERN's enterprise risk management and crisis management activities.
Design, organise and lead continuity exercises, simulations and stress tests; analyse outcomes and drive continuous improvement.
Provide expert advice to management and stakeholders on continuity strategies, disruption preparedness, recovery capabilities and resilience measures.
Develop guidance, methodologies, tools and training to build business continuity awareness, culture and capabilities across CERN.
Monitor, review and report on the effectiveness of business continuity arrangements and maturity.
Contribute to organisational resilience initiatives and continuous improvement activities within OSI-ICS.
Such other tasks as required for fulfilment of the Business Continuity Lead function.

En tant que Cheffe ou Chef de clinique titulaire d’un titre de spécialiste en néphrologie, vous assurez les activités cliniques à tour de rôle en néphrologie ambulatoire, hospitalière, hypertension, en dialyse ou en transplantation.
Vous faites preuve de résilience, de sens clinique et d’une grande capacité d’analyse dans la prise en charge de situations parfois complexes. Grâce à votre sens de l’organisation et à votre capacité à prioriser, vous assurez efficacement vos activités cliniques tout en répondant aux multiples sollicitations (patients et patientes, téléphones, correspondances, réunions).
Vous évoluez dans un environnement exigeant, à l’interface des soins, de l’enseignement et de la recherche. À ce titre, vous collaborez étroitement avec l’ensemble de l’équipe médico-soignante et veillez à une communication claire, fluide et respectueuse, tant avec vos collègues qu’avec les patientes et patients, en adaptant votre discours à leur compréhension.
En vous appuyant sur votre esprit d’équipe, vous faites preuve de solidarité face aux imprévus. En tant que cheffe ou chef de clinique, vous participez activement à la supervision et à la formation des médecins internes du département de médecine dans le domaine de la néphrologie et hypertension, en adoptant une posture de mentorat et en partageant votre expertise. Vous avez une activité de première ligne. Vous assurez les activités d'enseignement dans le domaine de la néphrologie (AMC, Forum, UIDC, APP, examens, stagiaires).

Introduction
You will ensure the availability and reliability of CERN's cryogenic installations by providing daily technical support, maintaining industrial instrumentation systems and diagnosing complex electrical faults. You will also contribute to the design and optimisation of low-voltage electrical cabinets and components, in compliance with electrical safety standards.
Functions
Contribute to the technical design and development of electrical cabinets for cryogenic systems, including the calculation to dimension the electrical systems, producing detailed electrical drawings, selecting components and ensuring compliance with electrical safety requirements.
Participate in and supervise the fabrication, installation and commissioning of electrical and instrumentation systems for cryogenic installations, including related procurement activities such as evaluating cost estimates and ordering component.
Provide daily operational support for cryogenic installations and contribute to the stand-by duty service to resolve urgent issues (including fault-finding, implementation of fixes, and reporting to the operation team).
Plan and coordinate preventive and corrective maintenance activities for system components, setting maintenance priorities and keep the corresponding technical documentation and procedures up to date.
Select and implement industrial instrumentation systems and carry out equipment testing and calibration according to operational requirements.

Introduction:
You will take responsibility for the maintenance and further development of several key existing beam instrumentation systems. As automation, AI and ML continue to transform scientific computing and software engineering, you will play a major role in the coordination of our group’s efforts as we embark on an ambitious programme to apply these technologies to accelerator instrumentation, data analysis, software development, and system operations.
Functions:
Collaborate with experts, operators, and multidisciplinary teams to understand needs, gather requirements, and develop effective software solutions.
Contribute to the adoption of modern AI-assisted software development tools and practices in collaboration with colleagues across CERN.
Maintain, support, and continuously improve existing beam instrumentation software systems.
Design, develop, test, commission, and maintain new and upgraded real-time software systems.
Contribute to knowledge sharing within the team and, where appropriate, supervise and mentor students or early-career talent.
During Long Shutdown 3, you will contribute to major modernisation activities, including:

En tant que cheffe ou chef de clinique titulaire du titre de spécialiste en chirurgie orthopédique, vous rejoignez l’unité de chirurgie du rachis dans le cadre d’une spécialisation. Elle bénéficie d’une reconnaissance internationale, particulièrement dans les domaines de l’endoscopie rachidienne, de la chirurgie des déformations complexes et de la traumatologie du rachis.
Dans cette fonction, vous assurez une activité clinique complète, incluant les interventions chirurgicales et la prise en charge des patientes et patients intrahospitaliers. Vous contribuez également activement aux projets de l’unité.
Vous faites preuve de rigueur, de sens clinique et d’une grande capacité d’analyse dans la prise en charge de situations parfois complexes, y compris dans la gestion des complications à court terme. L’activité clinique s’inscrit dans un parcours de formation postgraduée structuré et exigeant, visant la spécialisation en chirurgie de la colonne vertébrale. Introduction
Are you a skilled and experienced electronics engineer? Do you want to work in one of the world’s leading scientific Intergovernmental Organisations? Come and join a unique environment whose core value is excellence, and whose defining characteristic is teamwork. CERN, take part!
You will work in the TS-Group within the HSE Unit, which is responsible for occupational health and safety, including radiation protection, environmental protection, and emergency preparedness and response. Activities cover the monitoring and reporting of the environmental and radiological impacts of the Organization’s activities. 
In your role as an electronics engineer, you will be involved in the development and improvement of radiation and environmental monitoring solutions. This includes participating in the full lifecycle of hardware and embedded firmware development using modern methodologies and technologies.
Functions
Design and develop mixed-signal electronics, with a focus on analogue sensor interfaces and ultra-low-current measurement circuits.
Develop and maintain embedded code in VHDL and C to support system control, data processing, and hardware interfacing.
Consolidate and maintain heterogeneous firmware and its development environment (tools, build flow, and supporting infrastructure).
Adapt the MPSoC architecture to support the required communication interfaces and onboard processing.
Develop and integrate firmware updates to meet system functional and performance requirements.
Perform functional tests to verify correct system behaviour under expected operating conditions.
Develop dedicated electronic test boards and complex test benches to evaluate electronic systems under radiation at CERN and at external irradiation facilities.
Characterise newly developed systems through measurement, analysis, and validation activities to ensure compliance with functional and performance requirements.
Identify issues during testing, troubleshoot root causes, and implement corrective improvements.
Collaborate with hardware, firmware, and software teams to ensure effective system integration and reliable operation.
Ensure proper documentation, version control, and traceability of developments using collaborative tools such as GitLab and Jira.

Join CERN's detector R&D program for future high-energy physics experiments, working on advanced optical communication technologies for next-generation particle detectors. Your work will include hands-on laboratory characterisation of Silicon Photonics circuits and the design of innovative photonic devices. This position offers the opportunity to work at the intersection of photonics, electronics, and particle detection technologies.
Your responsibilities
Contribute to the electro-optical characterisation of custom-designed photonic integrated circuits (PICs).
Validate the PIC measurement results against optical simulations.
Support the integration and evaluation of PICs with particle readout chips (ROCs).
Prototype and demonstrate coarse wavelength-division multiplexing (CWDM) data-transmission systems.
Characterise and benchmark different data-link architectures.
Simulate and design a new generation of test PICs based on measurement results from existing PICs.
Present the progress to project meetings and conferences.
Document measurement and simulation results and methods.
Your profile
Proven experience in design and simulation of photonic components and integrated photonic circuits.
Experience in laboratory characterisation of optical and photonic components using OSAs, tunable lasers, and power meters.
Proven experience in high-speed electro-optical measurements utilising pattern generators, oscilloscopes, error detectors, VNAs, and spectrum analysers.
Hands-on experience in automation of measurement setups for opto-electronic devices.
Extended experience in analysis and interpretation of experimental and measurement data.
Skills
Expert user of photonic simulation tools (e.g., Ansys Lumerical, Synopsys RSoft).
Proficient user of electronic and optical laboratory instrumentation, including high-speed measurement techniques.
Expert user of C-based programming languages or Python.
Expert in data analysis and visualisation using Python, MATLAB, or equivalent.
Familiar with Linux-based development environments.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.

a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;

You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

The Oncology Data Science team in Biomedical Research at Novartis works at the intersection of oncology drug discovery, computational biology, AI/ML, and data engineering. We are seeking an enthusiastic AI/ML scientist with deep expertise in digital pathology and a strong curiosity for translational research to join the AI & Innovation Team.
This role will apply advanced AI approaches to generate insights from complex imaging datasets and support our oncology drug discovery programs.

 
Job Description
Key responsibilities:
Develop and apply AI / deep learning approaches to extract insights from digital pathology imaging datasets (e.g., H&E, IHC, mIF, Spatial transcriptomics).
Work with foundational models, including pre-trained, self-supervised, multi-purpose, and multi-modal models to advance generative AI applications in drug discovery.
Support imaging biomarker development efforts by analyzing pathology imaging data and collaborate with pathologists and translational teams to interpret image-derived biomarkers and biological findings.
Contribute to evaluation, validation, and benchmarking of image analysis algorithms and workflows.
Perform tissue segmentation, cell phenotyping, feature extraction, and spatial analysis using state-of-the-art computational approaches.
Stay current with advances in computational pathology, AI/ML, and spatial biology technologies; contribute to scientific publications; and present results at internal and external scientific conferences.

Requirements:
Ph.D. in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Computational Biology or related field. Candidates with MSc in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Computational Biology or related field, with 4+ years of relevant industry experience will also be considered.
Strong experience analyzing pathology imaging modalities including H&E, IHC, multiplex IF, and / or spatial transcriptomics data.
Understanding of machine learning methods for segmentation, classification, detection, and representation learning.
Experience in one or more of the following areas: generative AI, digital pathology foundation models, geometric deep learning and / or multi-modal learning.
Excellent programming skills and proficiency in deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch, with openness to learning new tools and technologies.
Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to communicate complex data insights and recommendations to cross-functional teams.
Strong research skills, evidenced by publications in leading scientific journals and / or conference presentations.

Rewards 
At Novartis, we’re committed to reimagining medicine together - and rewarding the people who make it happen. 

The rewards of being part of our team go far beyond base pay and incentives. We also offer a variety of competitive benefits in kind to help you thrive personally and professionally, such as insurance plans, retirement plans, wellbeing resources and global recognition programs. In addition, we provide flexible and hybrid working options, where possible, and a minimum of 14 weeks paid parental leave. 

Expected Annual Base Salary Range for role:

Join CERN's EP-ESE-ME section in the development of a radiation-tolerant microcontroller ASIC for use in future particle physics detectors and accelerator systems. Operating in highly challenging radiation environments, these systems require robust and reliable embedded electronics.
The project is based on an open-source RISC-V processing core and the CERN SOCRATES (System-On-Chip Radiation-Tolerant Ecosystem) framework for fault-tolerant SoC design. The successful candidate will contribute to the full development cycle, from requirements definition and system architecture to implementation, verification, and post-silicon validation.
Your responsibilities:
Analyse application requirements across CERN's accelerator complex and particle physics detector systems to define technical specifications for the microcontroller ASIC.
Contribute to the architecture, design, and validation of a radiation-tolerant microcontroller ASIC implemented in 65 nm or 28 nm CMOS technology.
Support the definition of the SoC architecture, including the selection and configuration of an appropriate RISC-V processing core.
Design, integrate, and validate peripheral IP blocks within the CERN SOCRATES framework.
Apply fault-tolerant design methodologies, including triple modular redundancy (TMR) and single-event upset (SEU) mitigation techniques.
Participate in design verification activities and physical implementation, from RTL development through to tapeout.
Contribute to post-silicon testing, characterisation, and validation following chip fabrication.
Your profile:
Strong understanding of digital logic design.
Solid experience with digital IC design and RTL development (Verilog/SystemVerilog).
Familiarity with standard ASIC design flows (synthesis, place and route, timing closure).
Knowledge of RISC-V architecture and its ecosystem.
Experience with microcontroller-based embedded systems development, including firmware programming in C and peripheral interfacing.
Skills:
RTL design and simulation (Verilog / SystemVerilog).
Familiarity with the digital ASIC design flow, including synthesis, place-and-route, timing closure, and sign-off activities.
Knowledge of fault-tolerant design techniques and radiation effects in CMOS circuits is an asset.
Microcontroller embedded systems development (firmware in C, peripheral interfacing, bare-metal programming).
Scripting and automation (Python or equivalent).
Linux/Unix working environment.
Curiosity and willingness to learn in a multidisciplinary environment.
Ability to work independently as well as within a team.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
You have a professional background in Electronics Engineer (or a related field) and have either:
a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;
or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

The Vacuum, Surfaces and Coatings (VSC) Group within CERN's Technology (TE) Department is responsible for the full lifecycle of accelerator vacuum systems, from development and design through to installation, operation and maintenance. The group operates facilities for measuring vacuum performance, assessing the compatibility of materials and surface technologies, and performing thin film coating, surface finishing, and vacuum-related physical and chemical characterisation.
As part of this group, you will join the Surface Coating and Chemistry (SCC) section, which provides CERN-wide expertise and services in wet surface treatments, surface and chemical analysis, and surface coating using physical vapour deposition techniques. In this role, you will contribute to the development of coating systems, thin-film materials and plasma-based surface treatments, with a particular focus on applications related to superconducting radiofrequency (SRF) cavities and adjacent technologies.
Your responsibilities
Deposit superconductive (thin) films onto various copper substrates (1.3 GHz, 400 MHz, 800 MHz cavities) via HiPIMS.
Perform plasma-based surface treatment for cleaning and surface passivation/functionalisation.
Perform in situ plasma diagnostics for process R&D (e.g. mass spectrometry, OES, Langmuir probe).
Perform materials characterisation and data analysis (e.g. SEM, XRD, XRF, profilometry).
Investigate the use of a dielectric barrier as a method for suppressing thermoelectric currents.
Commission and operate a movable cathode sputtering system for 1.3 GHz cavities.
Contribute to the design of new sputtering systems.
Prepare coating systems within a cleanroom environment.
More information here. 
Your profile
Practical laboratory experience in plasma-based thin film deposition, particularly HiPIMS.
Practical experience working with UHV systems.
Planning and executing experimental work, troubleshooting equipment or process issues, and analysing characterisation data to support coating development and optimisation.
Preparing technical procedures, documenting experimental methods and results, and contributing to safe, reproducible laboratory practices.
Working in a dynamic technical environment.
Participating in technical meetings, seminars, and project discussions, sharing findings and communicating technical information within and outside the organisation.
Using plasma diagnostic techniques in the context of thin film fabrication would be an advantage.
Experience working in a cleanroom would be an advantage.
Experience performing Rietveld refinement would be an advantage.
Skills
